This paper examines Constraint Handling Rules (CRCs), an extension of CRs that allows atoms in the heads to contain variables. We demonstrate that the atoms within these rules can be treated as constraints, enabling the use of constraint solvers to identify solutions. We define a subclass of CRCs where the number of atoms in each rule head is bounded by a constant, proving that this restricted variant possesses the same expressive power as standard CRs. Furthermore, we explore the implications of this finding for the complexity of constraint solving in CRCs.

We investigate the alignment of galaxy spin direction dipole axes within the SDSS-IV Extended Baryon Oscillation Spectroscopic Survey (eBOSS) across various redshift bins, utilizing a sample of 10,000 galaxies spanning $0.8 < z < 2.2$. Our analysis employs a Bayesian framework to test for the presence of alignment, specifically examining whether the dipole axes of galaxies in a given redshift bin are correlated with those in adjacent bins. Our results indicate that the observed alignments are consistent with a null hypothesis, showing no statistically significant evidence for galaxy spin direction dipole axes. Furthermore, the measured alignment amplitudes are consistent with those found in the SDSS-III survey, suggesting that the magnitude of these dipoles remains stable across redshift.

Few-shot learning (FSL) has gained significant attention for its ability to learn from limited labeled data, yet existing approaches often struggle with two critical issues: the challenges of sampling and the impact of label noise. To address these challenges, we introduce Eigen-Reptile, a novel training framework that integrates the eigen-decomposition of the meta-learner with the Reptile algorithm. This method offers two primary advantages. First, by utilizing the eigen-decomposition of the Eigen-Reptile model, the framework can effectively capture the essential characteristics of the meta-learner, thereby mitigating sampling-related issues. Second, Eigen-Reptile incorporates a meta-learner that is robust to label noise, ensuring reliable performance even when training labels are imperfect. Empirical results on the miniImageNet dataset demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving a 2.5% improvement in 5-shot accuracy and a 3.0% improvement in 10-shot accuracy.

This study introduces a novel framework for predicting cognitive decline in Alzheimer's disease (AD) by integrating MRI-derived biomarkers with Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) scores. The proposed approach utilizes a deep learning architecture featuring a multi-task learning component to simultaneously predict MMSE scores and generate latent representations of MMSE. These representations are subsequently employed to forecast the progression of AD. The framework's efficacy was validated using the ADNI dataset, demonstrating that it outperforms both traditional methods relying solely on MMSE data and state-of-the-art techniques that ignore MMSE data entirely.

This study examines the field of AI Ethics by analyzing the most cited works in the literature. Our analysis reveals that ethical analysis within this domain is currently insufficient and must be fundamentally restructured. We propose a novel framework for conducting AI ethical analysis, which is subsequently applied to the design of an automated driving system. Additionally, we identify key challenges encountered during this analytical process.

The study of Boolean-closed full trio families of languages over finite words has been thoroughly resolved, with a notable finding that the family of context-free languages is the only decidable one. This paper extends the investigation to languages over infinite words. We demonstrate that the family of context-free languages over infinite words is the exclusive class that is both decidable and closed under Boolean operations and tandem powers. Furthermore, we identify a broader class of languages over infinite words that is also Boolean-closed and possesses the same property regarding a context-sensitive language subclass.

This study introduces a hybrid channel estimation framework designed to enhance the accuracy of deep neural network (DNN)-based channel prediction. By integrating the DNN with least squares (LS) estimation, the proposed hybrid approach leverages the strengths of both methods. Specifically, the hybrid scheme utilizes the DNN to forecast future channels based on past observations, while relying on the robustness of LS estimation to handle current channel estimation. Simulation results demonstrate that the performance of this hybrid scheme surpasses that of the DNN-based method alone.

Recent discrepancies between theoretical predictions and experimental observations for $V_{ud}$ and $V_{us}$ suggest potential deviations from the Standard Model. This work examines the impact of these discrepancies on the CKM unitarity condition, specifically within the context of a two-Higgs-doublet model featuring spontaneous $B-L$ symmetry breaking. Our analysis demonstrates that this framework can accommodate the observed anomalies, provided that the mass of the charged Higgs boson exceeds approximately 1000 GeV.

This study introduces a new network architecture designed for the semantic segmentation of infrared imagery. The proposed framework integrates dilated convolution layers with a multi-scale feature fusion module to enhance performance. The initial stage employs a lightweight feature extractor to capture essential characteristics, while the subsequent phase utilizes a multi-scale decoder to reconstruct comprehensive semantic details. Experimental results indicate that this model achieves state-of-the-art performance on the IR-SC-10K benchmark, delivering superior accuracy with significantly fewer parameters than competing methods. Furthermore, the architecture offers a flexible design that can be adapted to various infrared segmentation tasks.

Data views are frequently utilized to isolate private data from shared information, yet they often fail to achieve this separation completely. This paper investigates the task of inferring data views, specifically focusing on scenarios where views do not entirely succeed in distinguishing private from shared content. We introduce a novel framework for learning data views that maximizes the extraction of shared information while minimizing the leakage of private data. We present a learning algorithm that operates in polynomial time relative to the input size and prove that, under certain constraints, it yields an optimal solution. Additionally, we develop an approximation algorithm capable of handling views defined by arbitrary functions. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed methods effectively recover shared information with minimal leakage of private data.

This study examines the correlation between hot dust emission and the physical characteristics of galaxies within the local universe. Utilizing data from the Spitzer Space Telescope, we analyzed a sample of 1,000 galaxies with redshifts $z < 0.1$ and absolute $K_s$-band magnitudes brighter than $-21$. We measured the flux in the 160 $\mu$m band and compared it against the 24 $\mu$m flux to determine the ratio of hot dust emission to total far-infrared emission. Our findings indicate that the fraction of flux in the 160 $\mu$m band is strongly linked to a galaxy's radio luminosity, morphological structure, and star formation rate. Specifically, galaxies exhibiting higher 160/24 $\mu$m flux ratios are typically radio-loud, displaying irregular morphologies, and possess elevated star formation rates. Conversely, galaxies with lower ratios are predominantly radio-quiet, exhibit regular morphologies, and have lower star formation rates. These results suggest that hot dust emission is primarily driven by star formation activity in the most luminous radio galaxies.

Although recent advancements have propelled large language models (LLMs) to achieve human-level performance on numerous tasks, these systems often struggle to grasp the complexities of human moral reasoning. To address this, we introduce MORALCOT, a novel prompting strategy designed to enhance LLMs' comprehension of human moral logic. By utilizing Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning, MORALCOT leverages an iterative process where the model generates and refines its own moral arguments to better align with human standards. Empirical results indicate that MORALCOT significantly boosts GPT-3.5's ability to capture human moral reasoning, surpassing the capabilities of several baseline methods.

A valuation ring $R$ with a $p$-residue field can be described as the direct limit of discrete valuation rings where the uniformizers are $p$-powers and the residues are finite fields; these approximating rings possess the property that their modules are precisely those which remain injective under the subsequent approximating steps.

The Dirac equation in two dimensions is fundamental to describing both graphene and condensed matter systems. This paper introduces a novel numerical approach for solving the Dirac equation in this context, utilizing the Dirac operator's specific algebraic properties to achieve a second-order accurate, unconditionally stable scheme that is both explicit and computationally efficient. The method's stability and accuracy are demonstrated through von Neumann analysis, followed by rigorous numerical experiments that confirm these theoretical findings. Furthermore, the proposed technique is applied to investigate the behavior of Dirac fermions under various conditions, including the influence of external potentials, the creation of bound states, and the generation of the Aharonov-Bohm effect.

Model Predictive Control (MPC) has proven effective for solving complex, multi-agent cooperative driving tasks. This paper introduces a novel MPC-based framework for cooperative lane-changing, designed to manage interactions among multiple vehicles. The proposed approach utilizes a hierarchical architecture that integrates both longitudinal and lateral control strategies. Furthermore, the study incorporates a predictive model of surrounding vehicles to account for their dynamic interactions. Simulation results indicate that this method significantly outperforms conventional MPC techniques in terms of both efficiency and safety.

The rapid proliferation of social media has created a fertile environment for the dissemination of misinformation, which can significantly impact public health and societal stability. While individuals often rely on social cues to assess information credibility, the specific mechanisms driving these social influences remain poorly understood. This study investigates the role of social media in credibility perception through a large-scale analysis of Twitter data concerning the COVID-19 vaccine. The findings indicate that users' credibility judgments are heavily swayed by the perceived trustworthiness of the accounts sharing the content. Furthermore, the research reveals that the volume of retweets serves as a predictive indicator for subsequent credibility perception. These results offer valuable insights for developing interventions aimed at mitigating the spread of misinformation.

The Road of the Autonomous Driving (ROAD) initiative establishes a standardized framework for enabling autonomous vehicles to interact with road infrastructure. This paper introduces $\pi$-ROAD, an enhanced framework that integrates reinforcement learning to facilitate real-time, data-driven decision-making for network resource management. Specifically, $\pi$-ROAD dynamically allocates resources to connected vehicles to enable the real-time transmission of video feeds to roadside units, which then distribute them to end-users via edge computing. By leveraging a neural network trained on historical traffic and network data, the proposed approach predicts future demand and proactively manages resource allocation. Evaluations conducted on a real-world dataset demonstrate that $\pi$-ROAD significantly outperforms conventional static allocation methods, achieving a 10% reduction in average video streaming latency and a 20% reduction in average packet loss rate.

This study introduces a collaborative approach for managing multiple robots within a shared workspace. We developed a collision avoidance algorithm based on Artificial Potential Fields (APF) to prevent collisions between robots and obstacles. While this APF method effectively mitigates risks, it can cause path deviations and increase the robot's travel distance. To address this, we propose a new algorithm that integrates the APF collision avoidance strategy with a Breadth-First Search (BFS) technique. The BFS component is specifically designed to minimize the additional distance incurred by collision avoidance maneuvers. We evaluated the proposed algorithm's effectiveness through simulations involving two robots operating in a common environment.

The trajectory of urban development is being reshaped by the convergence of heightened autonomy and machine intelligence. This article examines how the widespread adoption of autonomous vehicles (AVs) will transform city infrastructure, arguing that such shifts will necessitate a fundamental redesign of the urban built environment.

This study investigates online caching with a predictive model, where requests are handled either from the cache or fetched from memory. We introduce a novel algorithm that leverages the prediction accuracy to achieve a competitive ratio of $1+\epsilon$, with $\epsilon$ being a function of the relative prediction error scaled by the cache size. Our approach further demonstrates that the prediction-based algorithm surpasses the optimal offline caching strategy when the relative prediction error is sufficiently low.

The Trilateral Attention Network (TrA-Net) is a recently introduced architecture designed for image segmentation, featuring a Trilateral Attention Module (TrAM) that integrates three distinct pathways: a spatial, a channel, and a combined spatial-channel attention mechanism. While TrAM effectively captures dependencies across both dimensions, the TrA-Net framework has not yet been thoroughly examined regarding the specific contributions of each attention path. This study investigates the individual roles of these three channels within the module. We propose a novel, lightweight, and efficient variant of TrAM that incorporates a new fusion strategy, the Multi-Stage Fusion (MSF) module. This module dynamically merges the outputs of the three attention paths, allowing the model to leverage the unique strengths of each pathway. Furthermore, we introduce a new attention variant called the Trilateral Attention Module with Multi-Stage Fusion (TrAM+MSF). Experimental results on the Pascal VOC 2012 and ADE20K datasets demonstrate that this proposed module outperforms the original TrAM and other state-of-the-art methods.

We examine the gauge structure of linearized supergeometry within the framework of the 11-dimensional superspace $M^{11|32}$. In this setting, gauge transformations are defined by their action on gauge fields, which correspond to the cohomology classes of a specific differential operator. We explicitly compute these gauge fields by applying the torsion constraints of supergravity to the Riemann-Cartan torsion. Our findings indicate that the resulting torsion constraints impose restrictions on the gauge fields that align perfectly with those derived from supergravity.

The quality of training data is a critical factor in determining the performance of learning models. While existing methods for data selection and rejection rely on the model's confidence levels, they often fail to provide specific insights into the individual training examples. This paper introduces a novel approach to data quality assessment that leverages the model's internal representations. By utilizing these representations, the method can not only evaluate the overall dataset but also offer granular feedback on specific examples, identifying the particular attributes that hinder model performance. We validate this approach through a comprehensive analysis of its efficacy in improving model outcomes.

We examine the quantum charge pumping mechanism in the quantum anomalous Hall (QAH) surface, attributing it to the non-abelian matrix Berry phase arising from adiabatic temporal modulation of the band structure. This non-abelian nature stems from the phase's dependence on the initial electron state, a factor that becomes significant when the initial state is not an eigenstate of the system's Hamiltonian. By incorporating this matrix Berry phase into the pumping current formula, we demonstrate that the resulting current is amplified by a factor exceeding the standard single-state contribution. This enhancement is particularly pronounced when the initial state is a coherent superposition of the two lowest occupied bands. Consequently, leveraging this non-abelian matrix Berry phase offers a viable pathway for developing high-efficiency topological photovoltaic devices.

We introduce the METRO family of language models, which are trained on a curated dataset of 100 billion tokens derived from Wikipedia and GitHub. These models are trained using a novel curriculum that prioritizes content complexity and linguistic difficulty, resulting in a 10x increase in training speed compared to prior methods. Despite being built on a 10 billion parameter architecture, they outperform significantly larger models on various benchmarks, including MMLU, MATH, and MMLU. Furthermore, the models demonstrate strong few-shot capabilities, with performance that scales effectively with the number of provided examples.

We introduce a protocol for determining the topology of quantum networks composed of interconnected quantum nodes. This approach relies on the execution of local operations and measurements at individual nodes, eliminating the need for prior knowledge of the network structure or the transmission of quantum states across the network. The method is demonstrated on a four-node system, successfully reconstructing its topology with a fidelity exceeding 90%.

This research investigates how to present visual encodings to non-expert audiences. We conducted a user study with 20 participants to assess the effectiveness of three distinct introduction methods: generic, domain-specific, and no introduction. The findings indicate that generic approaches are the most effective for explaining encodings to the general public, whereas no approach is best suited for those with domain expertise. Additionally, we observed that participants with domain expertise performed better overall when they had no introduction than when they received a generic one.

The study of many-body quantum systems has been significantly advanced by recent breakthroughs in optical manipulation of ultracold atoms. However, the detrimental impact of periodic driving on system order remains largely unexplored. This work investigates how Floquet heating influences the dynamics of a one-dimensional Bose-Hubbard model, revealing that the resulting order depends critically on the relationship between the system's quasienergy gap and the Floquet frequency. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the system's density profile can be utilized to engineer the gap between Floquet bands, thereby enabling the creation of novel many-body states.

Counterfactual reasoning is a powerful method for generating plans to achieve specific goals. This paper introduces a novel counterfactual framework that incorporates uncertainty regarding model parameters. We demonstrate that plans derived from such reasoning are more resilient when executed in environments where the underlying model deviates from the assumed one. To address the resulting complexity, we propose a streamlined algorithm that generates these plans by sampling from a Gaussian process prior. Experiments on the RoboCup 3D Soccer game show that this approach surpasses existing methods in both success rates and efficiency, particularly when the actual environment differs from the model used for planning.

This study introduces a novel, end-to-end neural network designed for urban sound classification, which integrates a novel attention mechanism with a standard CNN architecture. The model is evaluated on two benchmark datasets, US8k and ESC-50, achieving reported accuracies of 94.4% and 98.7%, respectively.

This paper introduces SCAMP-5, a new compiler designed for the ScaLAPACK framework. It features a novel architecture that facilitates the automatic generation of distributed code from high-level sequential descriptions. The study details the architecture of this new compiler, including its generator and the associated data partitioning strategy. Furthermore, the paper presents an analysis of Cain, a compiler that automatically generates distributed code based on existing sequential codes and SCAMP-5 distributions. It compares the generated code lengths against those produced by Cain and other compilers for specific test cases within the SCAMPS-5 suite.

We examine the generalized Witten effect within the framework of quantum gravity, specifically focusing on its influence on charged state spectra. The analysis demonstrates that this phenomenon imposes distinct and stringent limits on the mass spectrum of these states.

This study examines the challenges of learning Nash equilibria in extensive two-player games. We introduce two new variations of regret pruning that enhance the original methodology by employing a more robust regret estimator and integrating a learning rate. Empirical results indicate that these proposed variants outperform the original regret pruning technique. Additionally, our findings suggest that the proposed pruning variants are more effective than counterfactual regret minimization (CFR) when the number of iterations is limited.

We present a novel modal logic grounded in the possible states-of-affairs framework, which serves as a rigorous semantic basis for re-evaluating Aristotle's medieval modal syllogistic. This approach offers a fresh perspective on a previously unsolved segment of Aristotelian logic, specifically concerning the "impossible" syllogisms. By interpreting these as valid within our system, we provide a coherent explanation for their inclusion in the medieval corpus.

This study examines a scenario where classical and quantum processes coexist within a shared framework of indeterminacy. We demonstrate that violations of causal order can be certified by both quantum and classical types of causal inequalities, yet classical inequalities demand a significantly higher minimum detection efficiency to achieve a breach compared to their quantum counterparts. Furthermore, we prove that violating a specific family of quantum causal inequalities necessitates that the underlying physical system be at least three-dimensional.

This study introduces a dual-critic reinforcement learning framework designed to manage distortion and rate constraints within video encoding. The system comprises two distinct agents: one generates the motion vector (MV) and quantization parameter (QP), while the other determines the bit allocation for intra prediction. The bit allocation agent operates by selecting from a predefined set of probabilities, whereas the QP selection agent chooses a QP value from a continuous range. The framework's efficacy is validated through experiments on the YUV444 component of the High Efficiency Video Coding (HEVC) standard. The findings indicate that the proposed method outperforms traditional rate-distortion optimization techniques, achieving a 1.1% average PSNR gain at a constant bit rate.

We present a chemical model of the inner regions of protoplanetary disks, specifically focusing on the gas-phase chemistry of carbon and nitrogen. This study employs a new chemical network that accounts for the photo-ablation of carbon-rich grains, which serves as a crucial source for gaseous C-bearing species. Our findings indicate that this photo-ablation mechanism sustains a prolonged equilibrium cycle involving the formation and destruction of C$_2$H$_2$ and C$_2$H. This process is driven by the formation of C$_2$H$_2$ through the reaction of C$_2$H with atomic hydrogen, followed by its destruction via reactions with H$_2$O and OH. Additionally, we examine the impact of grain chemistry on the overall carbon cycle, demonstrating that while gas-grain interactions are not the primary driver of carbon chemistry in the inner disk, they are essential for regulating the abundance of key species such as HCN, C$_2$H, and C$_2$H$_2$.

This paper introduces NeuralCut, a deep learning framework designed to accelerate the branch-and-cut process for mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) by addressing the challenge of selecting cuts. Unlike conventional approaches, NeuralCut integrates cut selection directly into the solver workflow, eliminating the need for a separate, distinct call to the branching heuristic. The model employs a graph neural network to encode the problem's structure, with a subsequent feed-forward layer determining cut selection. Experimental results on the 2018 GECOMIN competition dataset demonstrate that NeuralCut surpasses existing benchmarks in cut selection performance. Furthermore, the model significantly enhances the overall solution speed of the branch-and-cut algorithm, achieving up to a 1.6x speedup compared to standard baselines.

The $T_d$-Mo$_{1-x}$Ir$_{x}$Te$_2$ system, which features a layered structure with $T_d$ symmetry, exhibits a superconducting transition at $T_c = 1.5$ K. This compound displays anisotropic superconductivity, characterized by a significantly lower upper critical field ($H_{c2}$) when measured parallel to the $c$-axis compared to the basal plane. Furthermore, the $c$-axis $H_{c2}$ shows a positive temperature dependence, a signature indicative of strong spin-orbit coupling (SOC). Notably, the $c$-axis $H_{c2}$ reaches its maximum value near $T_c$, a phenomenon typically associated with $s$-wave pairing. Additionally, the $c$-axis $H_{c2}$ is highly sensitive to magnetic field orientation, a behavior that aligns with the findings of the specific heat measurement. These observations collectively suggest that $T_d$-Mo$_{1-x}$Ir$_{x}$Te$_2}$ hosts $s$-wave superconductivity with $d$-wave-like anisotropy.

Duplicate reports are a prevalent issue in bug tracking systems, often causing significant delays in resolution. While traditional methods rely on manual keyword matching, they frequently miss semantically similar reports. This paper introduces a novel approach to automatically retrieve identical bug reports by integrating Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques with a Bayesian classifier. The proposed method was evaluated on a real-world dataset from a large open-source project, demonstrating that it outperforms conventional keyword-based search strategies.

We introduce an effective field theory for graphene that incorporates a gauge field and a scalar field, both exhibiting strong coupling. This framework elucidates the characteristics of the graphene phase transition, specifically the emergence of a mass gap in the gauge sector and the development of a scalar condensate. The theory is examined through the lens of the gauge coupling constant, $\alpha$, and the scalar mass gap, $m$. At the critical value where $m = m_c$, the gauge coupling $\alpha$ transitions from a perturbative regime to a non-perturbative one, marking the point of the graphene phase change.

This paper introduces a self-training teacher-student framework designed to enhance Named Entity Recognition (NER) performance. The framework leverages a robust pre-trained teacher model to guide a student model, which is trained on both original and augmented data. To generate data augmentation, the system employs a graph-based approach that identifies semantically related sentences within a corpus. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques across various NER datasets.

The tourism sector is a vital economic driver for many nations, making the analysis of travel-related social media data highly valuable for enhancing service quality and strategic planning. This study introduces a novel framework designed to automatically extract and analyze tourism content from social media posts. The proposed approach employs a deep learning model to detect location mentions within tweets, followed by a clustering algorithm that categorizes these locations into distinct groups. These clusters are then mapped onto a geographic information system (GIS) to visualize the distribution of tourism activity. The paper outlines the methodology and validates the framework using Twitter data concerning the 2019 Rugby World Cup, demonstrating its effectiveness in analyzing location-specific discussions during the event.

This study introduces a machine learning framework designed to forecast the effective properties of microstructured materials. The model predicts homogenized elastic responses for two-phase composites, varying by microstructure, constituent material properties, and applied strain levels. It utilizes a convolutional neural network trained on a dataset comprising 10,000 finite element simulations of random microstructures. The results demonstrate that the network can accurately estimate effective properties for unseen microstructures and material combinations, even when those constituents exhibit nonlinear behavior.

We investigated whether this migration could be attributed to a nearby companion by analyzing data from the VLT/SPHERE instrument. We introduce a geometric framework that connects the dynamics of a particle moving in a two-dimensional potential $V(r)$ with finite-energy geodesics on a sphere. This approach demonstrates that zero-energy states in the specified potential map directly to finite-energy free-motion states on the spherical surface. Furthermore, this method allows for the derivation of effective potentials for any potential $V(r)$ simply by calculating the geodesic curvature of specific curves within the corresponding Lobachevsky plane.

This study examines the count of non-trivial solutions within the non-local integro-differential equation
$$ -\mathrm{div}(G(x)\mathcal{I}^{s}(x,u,u_{x})) = \lambda f(x,u) $$
defined on a bounded domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^{n}$, subject to zero Dirichlet boundary conditions. Here, $f$ represents a superlinear, one-phase nonlinearity, $G$ is a non-negative function, and $\mathcal{I}^{s}$ denotes a singular integral operator. The analysis relies on the application of the variational method, specifically utilizing the mountain pass theorem and linking theorems.

This study introduces a novel approach to multi-object filtering that utilizes unlabeled data, specifically addressing the challenge of determining trajectories for newly detected objects. Unlike existing methods, our solution significantly expands trajectory estimation possibilities by incorporating a discrete-time Markov chain to model object birth and death probabilities. This mechanism allows for the probabilistic assessment of whether new detections correspond to existing tracks or represent new entries. Furthermore, our approach integrates a Multi-Bernoulli filter with a particle filter to estimate both object states and object-specific cardinality. Extensive simulations demonstrate that this method outperforms current state-of-the-art techniques, particularly in scenarios with high object densities.

This paper introduces a novel stability assessment criterion for large-scale power systems with high-penetration of power converters, utilizing a recently developed nonlinear framework. This framework employs a hybrid approach that integrates a reduced-order model of the power network with dynamic representations of the control systems governing the converters. The proposed criterion diverges from conventional small-signal stability assessments by evaluating the largest Lyapunov exponent of the system's linearized model, thereby offering a quantitative measure of the system's resilience to disturbances. Furthermore, the study examines the impact of converter control strategies on the system's stability characteristics.

This study introduces a novel signature forgery detection approach utilizing the deep learning framework of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). The proposed method is designed to be highly efficient, requiring no pre-existing training data, ground truth labels, or specific knowledge of the underlying signature characteristics. The authors demonstrate that detection accuracy is significantly enhanced by focusing on three core attributes of signature templates: distinctiveness, complexity, and repeatability. The paper concludes with a thorough analysis of these attributes and their impact on forgery detection outcomes.

This paper establishes a connection between Hardy sums and oriented geodesics, enabling the extension of Hardy sums to both real and complex orientations. By doing so, we derive fresh identities concerning these sums, including several that were previously conjectured.

Mobile applications are essential for daily life, yet their effectiveness relies heavily on customization to meet individual user needs. While many apps offer basic personalization, they often fail to provide the depth required for specific user requirements. This paper introduces a new framework designed to enhance customization by utilizing persistent contextual values derived from user interaction patterns. By tracking and storing these long-term behaviors, the system creates a comprehensive profile that enables mobile applications to adapt more accurately to personal preferences. The proposed model is validated through a case study involving a smart home environment, demonstrating its practical utility.

This study introduces a novel 3D pose estimation architecture designed to deliver real-time performance by leveraging a multi-scale feature pyramid. The system employs a dual-branch approach: the first branch utilizes a 2D convolutional neural network to detect human joints, while the second branch predicts the 3D spatial coordinates of these joints. To enhance accuracy, the model integrates a dedicated loss function that incorporates the 2D detection results into the 3D estimation process. Evaluation on the Human3.6M dataset demonstrates that this method surpasses existing state-of-the-art techniques, achieving a Mean Per-Joint Position Error (MPJPE) of 49.4 mm.

The AstroSat mission, launched in 2019, carries the Cadmium-Zinc-Telluride (CZT) Imaging Spectrometer (INS), a collimated instrument designed to detect X-ray sources in the 2–10 keV range. This study details the development of an analytical model for the INS collimator, which was validated using the known fluxes of bright sources like Cyg X-1, Sco X-1, and 4U 1608-52. The model was subsequently applied to estimate the flux of the Crab pulsar, yielding a value of $1.0 \pm 0.1$ photons cm$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$, which aligns closely with the established literature value of $1.1 \pm 0.1$ photons cm$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$.

We have recently introduced a refined chromomagnetic interaction (AMI) model that successfully reproduces the mass spectra of both diquark-antidiquark tetraquark states and mesons. This study extends the AMI framework to investigate the properties of doubly-heavy tetraquarks, specifically the $QQ\bar{q}\bar{q}$ and $QQ\bar{q}\bar{q}$ families. Our approach involves a comprehensive analysis of experimentally observed states, alongside predictions for several yet-unobserved candidates. Our results indicate that the AMI model effectively accounts for the mass spectra of these doubly-heavy tetraquark families, yielding parameter values that align well with empirical data.

This study examines the impact of higher-dimensional operators on the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) within the context of the triviality and instability scale. We derive updated bounds for the Higgs mass and the top quark mass, as well as constraints on the Higgs self-coupling, by incorporating higher-dimensional operator effects. Our analysis reveals that these effects can either tighten or loosen the established bounds. Specifically, we find that the bounds on the Higgs mass and its self-coupling are more significantly influenced by these operators than previously recognized. Furthermore, we demonstrate that a non-zero lower bound on the Higgs mass can be derived solely from the triviality and instability scale, even without relying on vacuum stability arguments.

This study demonstrates that the solution to the Hamilton-Jacobi equation yields the entropic displacement convexity associated with a Carnot group's log-Sobolev functional, thereby establishing a connection to the $\mathfrak{p}$-Talagrand inequality. Furthermore, we derive an equivalent $\mathfrak{p}$-Talagrand inequality for Carnot groups, contingent upon the validity of the corresponding Hamilton-Jacobi framework.

This paper introduces an Exponentially Weighted Divergence (EWD) estimator for univariate density estimation, which serves as an alternative to the Density Power Divergence (DPD) estimator. The EWD estimator offers computational advantages by relying on the density's probability density function (PDF) and cumulative distribution function (CDF) rather than requiring the estimation of the underlying density itself. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that the EWD estimator shares the same asymptotic properties as the DPD estimator. Furthermore, simulation studies indicate that the EWD estimator achieves performance comparable to the DPD estimator while exhibiting greater numerical stability and robustness.

This study introduces a new algorithm designed to enhance the quality of images captured by moving cameras. The approach involves a pixel-level analysis of the scene, distinguishing between static and motion-centric pixels to apply specific processing techniques. The method utilizes a multi-scale strategy that leverages the inherent properties of the Laplacian pyramid. The proposed algorithm is capable of processing both grayscale and color images. The paper details the algorithm's theoretical framework, implementation, and performance evaluation. The method is particularly effective in scenarios involving significant camera movement, such as those caused by handheld devices or vehicles. This work addresses the problem of finding the closest non-negative imaginary (NNI) system to a specified linear time-invariant model. The solution is derived by utilizing the concept of the nearest non-negative imaginary (NNI) system approximation, which is then modified to satisfy the constraints of the problem. The paper establishes the existence of the optimal NNI system and formulates the corresponding optimization problem. Furthermore, it presents an algorithm based on the Weierstrass canonical form to solve this problem, demonstrating its effectiveness through a numerical example.

Continual learning (CL) has recently gained significant attention in the field of End-to-End Automatic Speech Recognition (E2E-ASR). This paper presents a systematic investigation of CL in ASR, specifically focusing on the CL-ASR task where models are trained on a sequence of data streams. The study evaluates various CL strategies, including the recently introduced CL-ASR-Net, alongside established techniques like replay, distillation, and incremental fine-tuning. Experiments conducted on the TED-LS2 benchmark demonstrate that the optimal CL approach yields a 17% relative reduction in WER for new tasks compared to incremental fine-tuning. The research further examines the impact of distinct ASR architectures, ASR model scales, and the specific nature of the data streams. The authors also introduce a novel metric for assessing the difficulty of data streams, which correlates with the performance degradation observed in CL methods. The study concludes by highlighting the potential of CL to enhance ASR performance in resource-constrained environments. The corresponding code is hosted at https://github.com/rahul-singh12345/continual-learning-asr.

Code-switching, the intermixing of two or more languages within a single utterance, is prevalent in social media communication. While this phenomenon complicates sentiment analysis, it has been extensively researched in the context of English and German. This study investigates the efficacy of existing approaches for detecting code-switched sentiments in English and German Twitter data. We evaluate the performance of a state-of-the-art Transformer model against a standard BERT baseline. Our findings indicate that the Transformer model achieves superior accuracy compared to BERT for this specific task.

This study examines a three-loop seesaw framework that utilizes a scalar lepton doublet and a single right-handed neutrino to generate the observed neutrino masses. The model is characterized by a single free parameter, the mass of the right-handed neutrino, denoted as $M_N$. We demonstrate that the mechanism operates effectively across a broad spectrum of $M_N$ values, ranging from 10 TeV down to 1 GeV. Furthermore, the model accounts for the correct magnitude of the Standard Model's muon $g-2$ anomaly. A key prediction is the existence of a light scalar lepton with mass below 129 GeV. The analysis also explores the implications for the muon sector and neutrino mixing angles, concluding with an assessment of the experimental prospects for detecting this light scalar lepton.

Product-based Neural Networks (PNNs) are a machine learning architecture designed to handle categorical data, leveraging a specific structural layout to capture interactions between categories at varying orders of complexity. This paper introduces a new method for automatically determining the optimal PNN structure, utilizing a search algorithm grounded in the principle of minimizing the number of model parameters. The proposed approach is evaluated on both synthetic datasets and real-world datasets from the MIMIC-III database. The findings demonstrate that the selected structures consistently yield the highest predictive performance, with the method proving to be both computationally efficient and scalable.

This study examines active transmitting beamforming design for intelligent reflecting surface (IRS)-assisted networks, focusing on the impact of channel state information (CSI) uncertainty. We begin by establishing an optimization framework that maximizes the minimum signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) subject to total transmit power limits and per-IRS phase shift constraints. To address the resulting non-convexity, we introduce a novel alternating optimization approach that alternates between optimizing the IRS phase shifts and the transmit beamformer. Furthermore, we develop a low-complexity solution for the beamformer by leveraging the geometric mean decomposition (GMD) technique. To mitigate CSI uncertainty, we then formulate a second optimization problem that maximizes the minimum generalized signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (GSINR) under the same power and phase constraints. A corresponding GMD-based alternating optimization algorithm is proposed to solve this problem, alternating between IRS phase shifts and the transmit beamformer. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the proposed CSI-robust beamforming design significantly outperforms the design without CSI robustness in scenarios with high uncertainty.

Branch prediction is a critical component of modern CPUs, and while conventional static predictors are widely used, dynamic prediction methods leveraging deep learning have recently emerged. This paper introduces a novel dynamic predictor that integrates a deep neural network with a single-bit history register. Experimental results indicate that this approach outperforms traditional static predictors and matches the accuracy of leading dynamic predictor models.

This paper introduces a deep convolutional neural network designed to manage a camera for tracking a target of interest. The system operates by predicting the necessary pan, tilt, and zoom adjustments to ensure the target remains within the field of view. The proposed approach is evaluated against a baseline method that relies on a simple heuristic for camera management. The results demonstrate that the proposed model surpasses this baseline in both computational efficiency and tracking performance.

We examine the SOS model on the half-space $\mathbb{Z}^{d-1}\times \mathbb{N}$, where the boundary condition is given by a fixed profile $\tau$ on $\mathbb{Z}^{d-1}\times\{0\}$. This work establishes the existence of boundary conditions yielding non-normalisable boundary laws. Additionally, we demonstrate that the model exhibits a phase transition when subjected to a sequence of increasing profiles $\tau_n$ that converge to a limit $\tau$.

This study introduces a novel approach to characterize entangled two-photon resonance energy transfer (E2P) using ultrafast spectroscopy. The E2P process is defined by the simultaneous absorption of two photons, where the absorption of the first photon creates an excited state that is immediately followed by the absorption of the second photon. The efficiency of this process is quantified by the effective rate coefficient, $K_{E2P}$, which is derived from the temporal evolution of the ground-state bleach signal. The research demonstrates that $K_{E2P}$ is highly sensitive to the distance between the donor and acceptor molecules, as well as the electronic coupling between their excited states. Furthermore, the study establishes a method for calculating the two-photon absorption cross-section, $\sigma_{2p}$, from $K_{E2P}$, thereby enabling the investigation of E2P in systems where traditional single-photon spectroscopy is insufficient.

This study examines the strong coupling constants for the $a_0(1450)$, $a_0(1815)$, and $f_0(1815)$ mesons by employing light-cone quantum chromodynamics (LCQ) and comparing the findings with those derived from QCD sum rules and the $a_0(1815)$ and $f_0(1815)$ meson decay constants. The analysis reveals that the strong coupling constants obtained via LCQ fall within the range predicted by the QCD sum rules approach. Additionally, the decay constants for these mesons are computed, and the results are contrasted against the corresponding values for the $a_0(980)$ and $a_0(1450)$ mesons.

This paper examines how linear regression techniques, such as propensity score matching and subclassification, can guide the design of observational studies to enhance causal inference. We demonstrate that these methods generate "implied weights" for individual units, which can be utilized to construct weighted estimators of treatment effects. Our analysis establishes that these weights offer valuable insights into the underlying rationale of various regression approaches. Furthermore, we show that observational study designs derived from such models can significantly boost the precision of treatment effect estimation. Finally, we introduce a new class of regression models that yield implied weights capable of effectively mitigating bias caused by unmeasured confounders.

This study examines the impact of voltage source converters (VSCs) on grid dynamics. By modeling the VSC as a synchronous machine, the analysis investigates how VSCs can mitigate system oscillations through damping. The paper introduces a novel control strategy utilizing the rotor angle deviation to enhance oscillation damping. Furthermore, the work derives analytical expressions for the optimal gain and cutoff frequency of a power system's closed-loop response when equipped with a power system stabilizer linked to the VSC.

We introduce a theoretical framework for analyzing photon correlations in the emitted light of a collective atomic ensemble. This model is built upon a microscopic description of the atomic dynamics, which incorporates the collective atomic wave function and the associated mean-field interactions. By applying the Born-Markov approximation, we derive a master equation for the reduced density matrix of the atomic ensemble, which is then solved using a perturbative approach. This solution yields the two-atom emission rate, which is subsequently used to calculate the two-atom correlation function. Our analysis demonstrates that the light exhibits sub-Poissonian statistics in the two-atom regime, a phenomenon driven by collective atomic effects. Furthermore, we examine how the two-atom correlation function varies with the inter-atom distance and the inter-atomic time delay.

This study examines the stability of kinks within the context of the $\phi^6$ model. We demonstrate that internal modes significantly influence kink stability, suggesting that the standard static approximation may be insufficient for obtaining accurate results. Furthermore, we present a novel method for calculating the kink's self-energy, which incorporates the effects of internal modes.

Generalized parton distributions (GPDs) are essential for understanding the internal structure of hadrons, as they connect to various high-energy and high-momentum transfer phenomena, including exclusive hadron production, hadronic form factors, and parton distribution functions. This study examines the evolution of GPDs at next-to-leading order (NLO) within the light-cone gauge, utilizing the specific method of the Mellin space approach. We derive the corresponding evolution kernels and analyze their characteristics, subsequently computing the anomalous dimensions for GPDs at the NLO level.

Text classification is a critical natural language processing task with broad applications, including sentiment analysis and topic categorization. While recent advancements in deep learning have yielded promising results, these models often struggle with interpretability and generalization. This study introduces a novel approach to text classification that enhances generalization by incorporating discrete noise into the training process. This technique effectively shifts the model's decision boundary, thereby boosting classification accuracy. We evaluate this method across various datasets and architectures, demonstrating that it achieves superior performance compared to existing noisy training techniques. Furthermore, we assess the approach's impact on model interpretability, revealing that it strengthens the alignment between input features and output labels.

Polyp detection is a critical task in endoscopy, yet it remains challenging due to the small size of polyps, the need for high precision, and the presence of false positives. While recent advancements in video processing have shown promise, they often fail to fully exploit the inherent temporal information in videos. This paper introduces a novel approach for polyp detection that leverages channel-aware attention to aggregate features across both space and time. By utilizing this attention mechanism, the model effectively captures dependencies between channels and frames, thereby generating more robust spatiotemporal features. Furthermore, we propose a new loss function designed to enhance the accuracy of localization and classification. Experimental results indicate that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques, achieving superior performance in both localization and classification tasks.

This work introduces a sequential sampling approach that generates samples from a Gaussian distribution with a mean derived from a user-defined distribution. By tuning a spreading factor, it becomes possible to regulate the degree of oversampling. The sampling algorithm is proven to be both ergodic and positive recurrent, with a closed-form expression for its mean first passage time. Furthermore, the paper presents a discrete adaptation of this method and demonstrates its application in solving the optimal stopping problem.

This work establishes that the flat part of the algebraic de Rham cohomology within an abelian scheme defined over a discrete valuation ring exhibits a stratification. The irreducible components comprising this flat part are identified as translates of torsion cosets under the flat part of the generic fiber's algebraic de Rham cohomology. Leveraging this finding, we demonstrate that the flat part of the special fiber of the canonical model of the minimal regular model remains stratified.

Over the past twenty years, Very High Energy (VHE) gamma-ray observations have significantly reshaped our understanding of the Milky Way's high-energy gamma-ray sources. This review outlines the current knowledge regarding the origins of Galactic VHE gamma rays, focusing on the physical mechanisms driving this emission and the observational signatures that characterize these processes.

This study examines the well-posedness and optimal control of diffusion systems featuring nonlinear, nonlocal boundary conditions. Initially, the analysis addresses the existence and uniqueness of solutions for the diffusion equation within a bounded domain, subsequently extending these findings to parabolic systems. The second section investigates the optimal control problem associated with the aforementioned system, specifically focusing on identifying the existence and uniqueness of optimal controls. This is achieved by reformulating the optimality conditions as a coupled nonlinear system of partial differential equations, thereby establishing the existence and uniqueness of the optimal control pair.

We present a new method for classifying compact stellar systems (CSSs) that leverages deep learning to analyze their color-magnitude diagrams (CMDs). This approach utilizes a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to process CMDs generated from Gaia DR2 data, which includes both Gaia G-band and G_BP-G_RP colors. Our study classifies 1,000 CSSs into four categories: globular clusters, open clusters, ultra-compact dwarf galaxies, and globular cluster candidates. The model achieves an accuracy of 94.4% on the training set and 89.1% on the test set. Analysis of the results indicates that the CMDs derived from the G and G_RP bands hold the most critical information for classification. Furthermore, the model demonstrates robust performance even when dealing with incomplete datasets, achieving 89.1% accuracy with only 50% of the stars included.

Simulations are a potent instrument for the development of Recommender Systems (RSs). They enable the modeling of user preferences and the generation of ground truth data to evaluate RS performance. This paper introduces a simulation framework designed to model users with diverse preference structures, thereby facilitating the assessment of various Recommender Systems. The proposed framework is built upon the UCI Adult dataset, a dataset that, while not originally tailored for RS tasks, offers a rich set of attributes suitable for recommendation modeling.

This paper introduces a hypothesis testing framework applicable to distributions characterized by infinite mean or variance, utilizing truncated sample means. We establish the asymptotic normality of this test statistic and demonstrate its utility in detecting shifts in distributional parameters. Furthermore, we evaluate the test's performance through both simulated data and real-world datasets.

Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have proven highly effective for EEG-based Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCIs), yet their reliance on large datasets and high computational costs limits their practicality. To address these challenges, this study introduces a novel BCI framework that integrates a novel CNN architecture with a specialized pre-processing technique. The CNN component leverages a multi-scale convolutional approach to extract features across various scales, while the preprocessing module utilizes a Laplacian filter to generate a spatial graph. This graph is then transformed into a one-dimensional signal, which is processed by a one-dimensional CNN to classify EEG signals. Experimental results demonstrate that this proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques, achieving superior accuracy with fewer training samples and reduced computational complexity.

This study investigates the holographic framework for a massive scalar field within a noncommutative space, utilizing the $AdS/CFT$ correspondence. We derive the two-point correlation function for the scalar field and apply it to the holographic computation of the scalar's mass anomalous dimension. Our results indicate that the holographic mass anomalous dimension aligns with the conformal field theory prediction in the large $N$ limit.

This study examines the allocation of kidneys to waiting-list patients, a scenario characterized by significant uncertainty regarding organ and recipient viability. We introduce a comprehensive Markov Decision Process (MDP) framework that accounts for the stochastic nature of organ and recipient incompatibilities, a feature largely overlooked in prior research. By modeling incompatibilities as explicit state variables, our approach enables the rigorous analysis of policies designed to mitigate the risk of rejecting incompatible kidneys. We demonstrate that this method accurately captures the complexities of kidney transplantation, a claim validated through a comparative analysis with actual transplant data.

This study investigates the internal architecture of both Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) by examining how their respective hidden states align with input data. We introduce a novel metric for quantifying the similarity between these states and utilize it to compare HMMs and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, a specific type of RNN. Our approach involves training both models on identical datasets and evaluating their performance using perplexity. Subsequently, we apply our similarity metric to assess the alignment between the hidden states of comparable models. Our findings indicate that while models trained on the same data exhibit similar hidden state structures, they do not necessarily correspond to similar underlying states. Furthermore, we demonstrate that HMM hidden states are more akin to those of LSTM models than to other RNN variants.

This study examines weighted Bergman spaces $A^2(w)$ and $H^2(\varphi)$ defined on the unit disk $\mathbb{D}$, along with the weighted composition operator $W_{\varphi,B}$ acting between them. We establish the criteria for when such an operator is compact or belongs to the Schatten class $C_p$ for $0<p<\infty$. Additionally, we analyze the conditions under which $W_{\varphi,B}$ is a nuclear operator.

Compressing neural networks is a viable strategy for deploying AI on resource-constrained devices. This study evaluates various compression techniques for text classification, focusing on the trade-offs between model size and accuracy. We assess the impact of different compression methods on both vanilla and wide-architecture models, including BERT, DistilBERT, and RoBERTa. Our findings indicate that wide architectures achieve superior performance, while pruning offers the most balanced compromise between reduced size and maintained accuracy. Specifically, pruning a wide DistilBERT model by 50% yields the optimal balance, resulting in a 1.5 MB model that retains 99.1% of its original accuracy.

The article proposes a new category of specialist within high-energy physics known as the "Data Scientist." This role is envisioned to bridge the gap between experimentalists and software experts, offering a unique perspective that can significantly enhance data analysis, development of software tools, and interpretation of findings. The proposal further outlines potential methodologies for integrating data science concepts into the daily operations of high-energy phenomenologists.

We introduce generalized Howe curves, defined as certain curves that decompose into Richelot isogenies, and we establish their identity with specific smooth, non-symmetric curves possessing the property of being decomposable by composed Richelot maps. Furthermore, we provide an explicit formulation for the bi-canonical system associated with these curves.

We report the discovery of two magnetic hot subdwarfs, designated as LMC 1029+2054 and LMC 1030+2055, within the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC). These objects were identified through a systematic survey of the LMC's hot white dwarf population, utilizing the 2.6m Nordic Optical Telescope (La Palma, Canary Islands) and the 2.3m William Herschel Telescope (La Palma, Canary Islands). Both stars exhibit strong magnetic fields, with measured longitudinal magnetic field strengths of 10.5 ± 0.5 kG and 11.5 ± 0.5 kG, respectively. Spectroscopic analysis reveals that both stars are hydrogen-poor, with hydrogen abundances of log(NH/NHe) = -2.05 ± 0.05 and -1.95 ± 0.05. This finding contradicts current theoretical models, which predict significantly lower hydrogen levels for stars with these masses and evolutionary ages. Furthermore, the observed abundances of carbon, nitrogen, and oxygen deviate from model expectations, suggesting that the hydrogen-rich envelopes of these magnetic hot subdwarfs have been stripped by a mechanism other than standard stellar evolution.

This paper introduces a novel framework for analyzing errors in matrix approximation by leveraging invariant matrix theory. We demonstrate that error analysis can be framed as an optimization problem over the cone of positive semidefinite matrices, solvable via invariant functions. Specifically, we examine two error measures: one for positive definite matrices and another for Hermitian matrices. For the Hermitian case, we derive the optimal approximations of a positive definite matrix $A$ under both the Frobenius norm and the spectral norm. Our findings indicate that the optimal Frobenius approximation is a diagonal matrix containing the first $k$ eigenvalues of $A$, whereas the optimal spectral approximation is a diagonal matrix with the first $k$ singular values of $A$. Additionally, we establish a novel upper bound for the Frobenius norm of a Hermitian matrix's off-diagonal block, expressed in terms of its spectral norm.

This study examines the relationship between wikitext and rendered HTML in Wikipedia by analyzing the frequency of specific tokens and the distribution of hyperlink attributes. The research reveals that HTML pages contain a greater number of hyperlinks than their corresponding wikitext versions. Additionally, the data shows that certain hyperlink attributes are utilized more frequently on HTML pages than others.

We introduce a novel method for creating polar domains within twisted bilayers, which can serve as a promising avenue for advancing topological physics. By utilizing a twisted bilayer composed of two distinct polar materials, we demonstrate that a domain wall separating opposite domains in the bilayer can host a one-dimensional metallic channel. This channel arises from the interplay between the materials' intrinsic polar properties and the moiré superlattice structure. Specifically, the electronic states are confined to the interface due to the opposing polarization directions of the materials. Our analysis indicates that the resulting one-dimensional channel exhibits a nontrivial topological character, evidenced by the presence of a quantized topological invariant.

This study examines the propagation of electromagnetic radiation within a static, spherically symmetric universe characterized by a constant curvature. We derive the null geodesic equations for this spacetime and analyze the resulting light paths. Furthermore, we compare these geodesic equations with those of a flat universe to highlight their distinctions.

This study examines the behavior of colloids within a liquid crystal medium confined between a flexible, wavy wall and a rigid, flat one. The wavy wall features an alternating sequence of hills and wells, and its shape can be controlled by adjusting the applied voltage. The research investigates how these undulations influence colloid trajectories, specifically analyzing the effects of varying wall geometry, the system's hydrodynamic properties, and the strength of the liquid crystal's elastic interactions. The findings reveal that the observed trajectories are highly sensitive to the interplay between the wall's shape and the system's physical parameters.

Machine learning (ML) and quantum computing (QC) are increasingly vital in molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, offering significant opportunities to address the limitations of classical computing. This study demonstrates that integrating ML and QC methods can substantially enhance the efficiency of simulating rare conformational transitions. We introduce a novel framework that combines ML and QC techniques to explore the free energy landscape of protein conformations. This approach utilizes ML to identify key collective variables and employs quantum algorithms to calculate the potential of mean force (PMF) governing these variables. We validate this methodology using a simplified model of a dipeptide, successfully mapping its PMF and confirming the accuracy of our results. Furthermore, we examine the advantages of employing quantum computing in conjunction with ML for this specific task.

This study examines how the seasonal development of sea-ice thickness categories evolves in response to the opening of water areas, utilizing a simplified one-dimensional model. The framework incorporates a stochastic component to represent the variability in ice breakup and freeze-up timing. The analysis focuses on how this variability influences the seasonal progression of ice thickness categories. The findings indicate that variability accelerates the seasonal evolution of thickness categories. The research also investigates the impact of variability on the average number of days during which a specific thickness category exists. The results demonstrate that increased variability reduces the average duration of presence for any given thickness category.

Singing voice synthesis has evolved significantly over the past decade, yet it remains an unresolved challenge with substantial potential for both commercial and academic advancement. This paper introduces a novel singing voice synthesis framework based on the latent diffusion model. By employing a single encoder to derive style features from a reference voice, the system synthesizes a target voice conditioned on melody and lyrics, allowing users to generate singing styles matching the provided reference. Experimental results indicate that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches, delivering superior subjective quality alongside favorable objective metrics.

This study introduces NIPS4Bplus, an enhanced version of the NIPS4B dataset, which expands the audio recordings to a 10-minute duration and includes additional bird species. The collection process involved deploying autonomous recorders in various habitats across Europe, the UK, and New Zealand. The dataset comprises 100 hours of audio featuring 24 species, including 10 new additions, with 90 hours designated for training and 10 hours for testing. We also present a new baseline model for automatic bird species classification, achieving a 50.4% accuracy on the test set. Furthermore, we outline potential applications for ecoacoustic research and monitoring bird populations. The dataset and source code are accessible at https://github.com/ecoacoustics/NIPS4Bplus.

Frame-based event camera calibration is a critical prerequisite for extrinsic calibration between conventional frame-based and event-based systems. This paper introduces a novel framework that leverages the inherent motion characteristics of event streams to enhance the accuracy of this calibration process. By modeling event flow as a vector field, we derive a closed-form solution for estimating the camera's rotation matrix. Additionally, we develop a method to recover translation from the calculated rotation, utilizing a cost function that incorporates a new motion constraint. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach surpasses existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of performance.

Graph learning has proven effective across diverse domains, including social media, e-commerce, knowledge graphs, and biological networks. However, the field has largely overlooked the specific characteristics of citation networks. This paper introduces a new graph learning framework designed for academic citation graphs, which integrates graph neural networks with knowledge distillation. By leveraging the collective insights of multiple models, this approach enhances the quality of learned node representations. Empirical evaluations on two real-world citation datasets demonstrate that the method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques in both node classification and link prediction tasks.

The action of the four-strand braid group on exceptional collections within the degree 2 Hirzebruch surface is realized through an action on the K-theory of $\mathbb{P}^1$. This paper demonstrates that these braiding actions correspond to specific elements within $K(\mathbb{P}^1)$, specifically the third Chern classes of rank 2 vector bundles on $\mathbb{P}^1$. Furthermore, we provide a proof of this correspondence and offer a classification of exceptional collections up to braiding equivalence.

This study introduces a 3D guidance system for retinal surgery that utilizes a spotlight projector to orient the surgeon. By projecting a luminous beam onto the retina, the mechanism provides a visual cue that enhances depth perception. The proposed system relies on a 3D model of the eye, which is updated in real-time using data from a depth camera and a near-infrared (NIR) camera. To ensure the spotlight illuminates the target retinal area, the system calculates the necessary movement for the beam by determining the current and desired positions of the retinal target. These positions are derived by applying a transformation matrix to the 3D eye model, which is updated via stereo matching of the NIR camera images. The FIDO2 standard is a key driver in the shift toward passwordless authentication, enabling secure, user-friendly login experiences across various devices. This paper introduces a framework for analyzing the security of FIDO2 systems, specifically examining how the selection of cryptographic algorithms impacts overall system protection. By modeling FIDO2 as a layered architecture, the research demonstrates that security can be effectively analyzed at individual layers, with the system's total security determined by the weakest link. This paper examines the expressive power of the $\pi$-calculus by contrasting it with reactive Turing machines, a computational model designed to simulate Turing machines with infinite tapes. The method optimizes for minimum travel time while adhering to constraints on maximum acceleration, velocity, and angular velocity. The findings demonstrate that the proposed algorithm generates faster trajectories than polynomial approaches and achieves results comparable to those of established minimum-time optimization methods.

This study introduces a method for estimating the positions of low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites using inter-satellite measurements. The approach relies on a nonlinear least squares optimization framework, which is solved via the Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm. The paper demonstrates that localization accuracy improves when inter-satellite data is combined with ground station observations compared to using inter-satellite data alone. We employed a Bayesian framework to simultaneously determine the orbital period's decay rate and the transit timing offset, accounting for correlated noise in the light curve. Our findings indicate that the orbital period of XO-3b is decreasing at a rate of $-1.0^{+0.3}_{-0.2}$ seconds per year, a result that aligns with predictions from standard tidal models. These results suggest that the tidal dissipation in the rocky core of the planet is relatively low, a conclusion supported by the planet's high bulk density.

Our findings indicate that the method is highly effective at recovering true instrumental parameters, particularly when the prior is broad. Furthermore, we explore the method's resilience to systematic errors and its ability to handle complex, non-linear relationships between instrument parameters and detector responses.
