Multitask training has recently gained significant attention, offering a method to train models that learn multiple tasks simultaneously. Although this approach holds great promise, its widespread adoption remains limited due to a scarcity of experimental research. This study introduces a novel, systematic experimental framework for multitask training, which facilitates the exploration of a broader range of training strategies and enables the identification of optimal configurations. We demonstrate that this methodology can substantially enhance the performance of multitask models. Furthermore, we outline several novel techniques that achieve state-of-the-art results on the ImageNet benchmark.

This paper introduces TrafficSigns-HOG, a comprehensive dataset comprising 144,000 hand-crafted hand features extracted from 2,400 traffic signs sourced from the German Traffic sign Detection Dataset (GerSTD). We demonstrate that this collection of features facilitates transfer learning for detection algorithms, enabling them to achieve state-of-the-art performance on both traffic sign detection and classification tasks. Additionally, we present a novel traffic sign detection algorithm that leverages a pre-trained object detector and a sign-specific classifier. This approach attains a mean average precision (mAP) of 99.8% on the sign detection task and maintains a 99.4% accuracy rate on the classification task.

In recommendation systems, the scarcity of labeled data often hinders the effectiveness of supervised learning. To address this, we introduce SelfCF, a self-supervised framework designed to enhance recommendation accuracy and accelerate training. SelfCF operates by generating self-supervised tasks that create pseudo-labels for the original data. These tasks involve two components: a contrastive learning module that aligns user preferences with item attributes, and a contrastive reconstruction module that preserves item identity. By leveraging these pseudo-labels, SelfCF significantly speeds up the training process while maintaining or improving performance. Extensive experiments on three datasets demonstrate that SelfCF outperforms conventional supervised methods and existing self-supervised baselines. Furthermore, the framework exhibits robust generalization capabilities across different datasets, and its efficiency is further enhanced through the use of a lightweight encoder.

This article investigates the enumeration of covers within the context of ramified Riemann surfaces. We demonstrate that imposing supplementary ramification constraints can significantly alter enumeration outcomes, a phenomenon that counteracts classical results such as those by Harris and Mumford. Furthermore, we establish an explicit formula for the count of covers subject to multiple branching constraints.

This study investigates the high-energy behavior of the density of states and optical conductivity in a gapped Dirac semimetal. We demonstrate that, at elevated energies, these properties exhibit a universal dependence on the ratio of the photon momentum to the inverse of the gap magnitude. These findings are applicable to systems characterized by a gapped Dirac Hamiltonian, encompassing scenarios involving both single and multiple Dirac nodes.

This study examines a discrete slow-fast differential system characterized by periodic coefficients, applied to models of population dynamics. We demonstrate that under specific conditions, as the period approaches infinity, the system's behavior resembles that of a non-periodic counterpart.

Third-generation gravitational wave observatories, such as the Einstein Telescope and Cosmic Explorer, are anticipated to detect numerous binary black hole mergers. This study investigates the detectability of higher-order modes (HoMs) in these events, specifically focusing on the (3,3) and (4,4) modes. We employed the LALSimKAGRASimantO (LST) waveform model, which incorporates the effects of spin precession and recoil velocities, to generate simulated waveforms. These signals were analyzed using the 3D network of gravitational wave detectors, including the future detectors. We calculated the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) for the (3,3) and (4,4) modes, as well as the combined SNR for the (2,1), (2,3), (3,3), and (4,4) modes, to determine the probability of detecting these modes. Our results indicate that approximately 10% of binary black hole mergers will exhibit detectable (3,3) and (4,4) modes in third-generation detectors. Furthermore, the joint detection of the (2,1), (2,3), (3,3), and (4,4) modes is expected in roughly 20% of these mergers. These findings suggest that future detectors will be capable of observing higher-order modes in a significant fraction of binary black hole mergers.

Astrometric binaries serve as a promising method for discovering black hole companions, as the gravitational influence of a massive companion can be detected through the radius of curvature and orbital velocity of the visible star. This study introduces a novel approach to identify such binaries by analyzing the geometric characteristics of the astrometric orbit. We demonstrate that the radius of curvature can be derived from the orbital elements, and we establish a relationship between this radius, the orbital velocity, and the mass of the unseen companion. By applying these findings, we developed a new detection technique that utilizes the radius of curvature and orbital velocity to pinpoint astrometric binaries with black hole companions. This method was tested on Gaia Data Release 3 (DR3) data, yielding 1,000 candidate binaries. Subsequent cross-matching with Gaia Envelope (GEAS) data identified 100 of these candidates as confirmed binaries. Finally, we applied the Schwarzschild precession formula to calculate the Schwarzschild radius for each of the 100 confirmed binaries, revealing that the Schwarzschild radius exceeds 90% of the Schwarzschild radius of the visible star.

This study introduces a new hybrid genetic algorithm designed to address the 0/1 knapsack problem. It integrates crossover operators—specifically uniform, single-point, and two-point crossover—with selection techniques including tournament, truncation, and rank selection. By evaluating every possible pairing of these operators, the research identifies a superior combination that achieves the fastest convergence rate. Furthermore, the paper demonstrates the algorithm's effectiveness through comparisons with other genetic algorithms and various heuristics, utilizing both real-world and synthetic datasets.

This paper examines $L^2$ estimates for oscillatory integrals featuring a phase function that is a mixture of a smooth component and a singular, non-smooth one. We establish that the $L^2$ bounds for such integrals with hybrid phase functions differ from the standard results applicable to purely smooth phases or those with purely polynomial phases.

This study presents the University of Edinburgh's entry for the SemEval-2019 Hate Speech Detection task, specifically focusing on subtasks A (automatic hate detection) and B (automatic hate justification). For subtask A, we employed a BERT-based model that achieved an MAF1 score of 89.0 on the development set and 87.0 on the test set. For subtask B, we utilized a BERT-based model augmented with a linear classifier, securing an MAF1 score of 89.0 on the development set and 87.0 on the test set. Our subtask A model ranked 2nd, while the subtask B model placed 3rd in their respective categories.

We introduce a novel approach to enhance the computational efficiency of quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) calculations by utilizing a QMC-derived density functional theory (QMC-DFT) framework. This method leverages the rapid scaling of DFT to accelerate QMC force calculations, thereby enabling ab initio geometry optimizations and molecular dynamics simulations. The approach is validated through applications to various systems, including the hydrogen atom, hydrogen molecule, and solid silicon. Specifically, we demonstrate that the computational cost of QMC energies and forces scales with the square of the effective pseudopotential valence charge ($Z^2$). By utilizing the Hartree-Fock exchange approximation within the QMC-DFT setup, we achieve a reduction in the computational cost of QMC forces by approximately a factor of 100 for silicon. This strategy is highly promising for advancing QMC methodologies toward the study of larger and more complex systems.

This study examines the dissemination of claims regarding the 2020 US election's legitimacy and validity. By analyzing a collection of 1.2 million tweets, the authors investigated the circulation of specific narratives, including assertions of widespread voter fraud and evidence of a foreign influence campaign. The research further assessed Twitter's moderation responses to these narratives. The findings indicate that a significant portion of the analyzed tweets were linked to election-related misinformation, and that platform responses often mirrored these claims rather than countering them.

We demonstrate that for a generic $C^1$ flow on a compact Riemannian manifold, the set of points with maximal average expansion (points of maximum entropy) has a Hausdorff dimension equal to that of the flow itself under any SRB measure. This result extends the findings of Bowen (1979) and Brin-Katok (1985), which were originally established for Axiom A flows.

Deep Bayesian neural networks (DBNNs) are highly effective for uncertainty quantification, yet their computational demands often hinder practical application. To address this, we propose a novel framework for constructing efficient DBNNs by integrating variational autoencoders (VAEs) with the Bayesian neural network architecture. This approach enables the acquisition of latent representations for both inputs and outputs, effectively reducing the input and output dimensions. Furthermore, we introduce a specific loss function designed to maintain the integrity of the posterior distribution within the compressed latent space. Experimental results demonstrate that this method successfully maintains high predictive accuracy while significantly lowering computational costs.

We introduce a novel framework for electron transfer reactions that integrates the computational efficiency of Marcus theory with the accuracy of instanton theory. This approach is founded on a shared mathematical foundation: both theories rely on a path integral formulation where a particle traverses a complexified coordinate space. While instanton theory utilizes this to determine the free energy barrier for thermal reactions, our method applies the same path integral approach to nonadiabatic electron transfer, accounting for the quantum tunneling of nuclei through barriers. This is achieved by extending the coordinate space to include a nonadiabatic phase factor, $e^{iS_{\rm A-B}/\hbar}$, where $S_{\rm A-B}$ represents the action difference between the reactant and product states. The resulting formalism is both computationally efficient and highly accurate, as it utilizes the same mathematical machinery as instanton theory. We demonstrate the method's utility by calculating the tunneling splitting of the vibronic ground state in the hydrogen molecule and analyzing the kinetics of electron transfer in the photoactive yellow protein. Our results indicate that this method offers a robust and efficient tool for investigating nonadiabatic electron transfer, particularly in scenarios where nuclear tunneling plays a critical role.

This study introduces a novel approach for trajectory tracking in robotic systems, designed to mitigate the impact of unmodeled dynamics. The methodology integrates a model-based controller with a unifying framework that leverages the inherent structure of the robot dynamics alongside a unifying adaptive control scheme. This adaptive component is engineered to specifically target and compensate for a broad spectrum of unmodeled dynamics, including those arising from actuator nonlinearities. The paper further establishes the theoretical stability of the proposed system and validates its effectiveness through simulations on a six-degree-of-freedom robotic manipulator.

This study examines the electronic, thermoelectric, and thermopower characteristics of the $\text{La}_{0.85}\text{Sr}_{0.15}\text{CoO}_3$ alloy, which contains a tungsten-derived impurity band. The analysis utilizes a combination of experimental data and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Results indicate that the impurity band significantly influences the alloy's electrical conductivity and thermopower. Furthermore, the DFT model successfully replicates the observed behavior of the alloy's Seebeck coefficient, confirming that the impurity band plays a critical role in the material's thermoelectric properties.

This paper introduces a probabilistic framework for the "perfect sum" problem, which involves determining the likelihood that a sum of random variables equals a specific target value. We demonstrate that this approach offers significant advantages over conventional deterministic methods, which typically assume the target is achievable and often yield inaccurate results. The proposed technique is applied to three distinct scenarios: the sum of uniform random variables, the sum of random variables following a Poisson distribution, and the summation of random variables with a discrete distribution.

This article introduces a deterministic algorithm designed to identify an element of degree $m$ within the extension field $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$, where $m$ is a prime divisor of $q^n-1$. The method's efficiency is contingent upon the irreducibility of the polynomial $x^m-a$ over the base field $\mathbb{F}_q$. Additionally, we provide an analysis of the algorithm's performance and illustrate its application in the context of the $n$-sequence.

Over the past few decades, model checking has emerged as a highly effective method for verifying the correctness of software systems. This paper examines the evolution of model checking technologies and their significant impact on the development of algorithms for synthesizing parallel strategies.

Optimized metasurface imaging systems offer a promising avenue for miniaturizing optical imaging devices. However, the performance of these systems is often hindered by noise, which can degrade the accuracy of the optimization process. This study introduces a new optimization framework designed to enhance the robustness of metasurface imaging systems against noise. By integrating a new loss function with a Bayesian optimization approach, we achieve highly robust designs. The proposed method demonstrates superior performance compared to traditional optimization techniques, successfully recovering images with a high signal-to-noise ratio of 30 dB. The research further validates the approach by designing and testing a functional robust imaging system.

We present a theoretical investigation into the excitation of hydrogen atoms to Rydberg states via a two-step laser process. The initial step involves populating an intermediate excited state using a laser tuned to the $1s \to 2p$ transition, followed by ionization to the Rydberg manifold through a second, weaker laser pulse. Our analysis demonstrates that this sequential mechanism is highly effective for generating high-angular-momentum Rydberg states, particularly when utilizing a short-duration, low-intensity second laser. We further examine the influence of the second laser's polarization on the resulting Rydberg state angular momentum and provide a theoretical framework for understanding the selection rules governing this two-photon excitation.

Semi-supervised learning (SSL) has garnered significant attention recently, with numerous methods leveraging unlabeled data to enhance model performance. However, these approaches often fail to fully exploit the potential of unlabeled data, as they typically rely on a single image per sample. This study introduces a novel SSL framework that utilizes augmented samples derived from multiple images to enrich the unlabeled dataset. Specifically, we propose a Multi-View Consistency Learning (MVC) approach that enforces consistency across these different views. VC further employs a consistency-based pseudo-labeling strategy to assign labels based on this multi-view agreement. Experimental results on the SVHN and CIFAR-100 datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art SSL techniques, achieving a 1.5% improvement on SVHN and a 2.5% improvement on CIFAR-100.

This study introduces a novel framework for designing experiments to investigate stochastic gene expression, leveraging the utility of mathematical models. We propose a sequential design methodology that integrates the mathematical model with experimental outcomes to derive a Bayesian posterior distribution regarding the model's parameters. Subsequently, we utilize this distribution to calculate the expected utility of potential experimental designs, thereby selecting the optimal approach. This methodology is applied to a specific model of transcriptional regulation, demonstrating that our technique can identify an optimal design capable of precisely estimating the model's parameters.

Graph neural networks (GNNs) have recently emerged as a potent class of models for learning from graph-structured data. However, selecting appropriate GNN architectures remains a difficult task, as the vast number of hyperparameters makes manual tuning laborious and often suboptimal. This study introduces a novel framework for learning GNN hyperparameters by framing the problem as a graph-to-graph translation task. By training a model to predict the optimal hyperparameters for a target graph based on a source graph, we demonstrate that this approach can automatically discover superior configurations. Experiments on various graph classification benchmarks reveal that our method not only achieves higher accuracy than existing baselines but also identifies novel, high-performing hyperparameter settings.

Quantum algorithms offer significant promise for addressing computationally demanding tasks, yet their practical implementation on near-term hardware is constrained by noise. This study examines the impact of coherent dephasing errors on the training dynamics of the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA). We demonstrate that, under specific conditions, the training trajectory can be enhanced by deliberately introducing such dephasing errors. To evaluate the training behavior, we apply the methodology to the MaxCut problem, utilizing the maximum overlap between the final state and the solution manifold as a performance metric. Our findings indicate that the inclusion of engineered dephasing errors can accelerate convergence, thereby improving the quality of the final state.

Person Re-Identification (Re-ID) has become a prominent topic in computer vision due to its practical value in security and surveillance. However, existing Re-ID methods often struggle with severe occlusion and pose variations, largely because they fail to fully exploit the inherent 3D structure of pedestrian data. To address this, we introduce a novel framework that leverages 3D information for person Re-ID. Our approach utilizes a 3D-aware feature learning strategy to capture pose-invariant features, alongside a 3D-aware attention mechanism to focus on occlusion-robust body parts. Specifically, we employ a 3D-aware feature learning module that integrates 3D-aware attention to isolate occlusion-robust features, and a 3D-aware attention module that identifies pose-invariant body parts. Additionally, we incorporate a 3D-aware contrastive learning strategy to enhance feature discrimination. Extensive experiments on standard benchmarks demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art results, with the code available at https://github.com/3d-reid/3d-reid.

This study introduces a novel approach for generating high-fidelity synthetic time series data for power systems. By integrating the strengths of both deep learning and traditional statistical methods, the proposed framework utilizes a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) to learn the latent space representation of the data. Subsequently, a Conditional Autoregressive Generative Adversarial Network (CARGAN) is employed to synthesize high-resolution data from this latent space. The resulting dataset exhibits strong statistical similarity to the original series while offering enhanced data quality. Furthermore, the approach is designed to be computationally efficient, making it suitable for real-time applications.

This study examines the convergence behavior of perturbed iterative methods applied to variational inequality problems within Banach spaces. We demonstrate that, provided certain conditions are met, the iterative process modified by perturbations will converge uniquely to a solution. Furthermore, we establish convergence theorems for sequences generated by unperturbed processes. Additionally, we apply these findings to analyze the convergence of both perturbed and unperturbed iterative methods specifically designed for solving the sign norm problem.

The text discusses a conjecture concerning hyperbolic element axes within arithmetic Fuchsian groups, verified for groups derived from quaternion orders over imaginary quadratic fields. This supports the broader conjecture, applicable to all such groups, that the proportion of hyperbolic element axes remains bounded away from infinity.

This study examines the potential decay of the $\rho$ quark into a $Z$ boson and a gluon, a process hypothesized to arise from the spontaneous breaking of a $\mathbb{Z}_3$ symmetry. Utilizing LHC data from the ATLAS detector, specifically from 13 TeV proton-proton collisions with an integrated luminosity of 139 fb$^{-1}$, we search for this decay by analyzing the $\ell^+\ell^-$ + jets final state, where $\ell$ represents an electron or muon. No evidence for a signal was found, leading to 95% confidence-level upper limits on the $\rho$ quark production cross-section. These constraints exclude new physics at energy scales exceeding 10 TeV, contingent on the $\rho$ quark being produced via gluon fusion.

Pd$_3$P$_2$S$_8$ represents a newly discovered superconductor with a critical temperature ($T_{\mathrm{C}}$) of 1.5 K. This study examines the pressure dependence of $T_{\mathrm{C}}$ within the range of 0–1.5 GPa using resistivity and magnetization measurements. The results indicate that $T_{\mathrm{C}}$ rises with pressure, reaching a peak of 2.0 K at 1.5 GPa. Furthermore, the magnetization data reveal a pressure-induced enhancement in the superconducting critical field ($H_{\mathrm{c}}$). These findings suggest that Pd$_3$P$_2$S$_8$ possesses a robust superconducting mechanism, potentially driven by strong electron-phonon interactions.

We demonstrate that an infalling observer experiences a black hole horizon as a smooth transition, maintaining coherent quantum states and avoiding the firewalls predicted by the AMPS paradox. This smooth geometry is supported by the absence of high-energy particle fluxes in the exterior spacetime. Crucially, we show that once an observer crosses the horizon, their duration of experience before eventual evaporation and disappearance is limited to the logarithm of the black hole's mass measured in their own proper time.

Neural ordinary differential equations (ODEs) serve as a potent tool for modeling vector fields from noisy data, a technique with broad applications in science and engineering. However, these models often fail to capture the full complexity of real-world systems, which are typically high-dimensional and exhibit chaotic behavior. This study introduces a new framework for training neural ODEs that integrates the Koopman operator theory. This approach enables the model to represent high-dimensional nonlinear dynamics through linear representations in an expanded, high-dimensional state space. We validate this methodology using a high-dimensional Lorenz-like chaotic system, demonstrating that the proposed framework successfully recovers the system's dynamics.

Instruction tuning has proven highly effective for enhancing the downstream performance of large language models. Nevertheless, this process involves a complex interplay of various factors, including the model's size, the specific task domain, and the quality of training data. Consequently, it is not guaranteed that a model will consistently improve across all tasks after being instructed. To address this, we introduce a novel framework designed to analyze the performance trade-offs inherent in instruction tuning. Our approach involves a systematic examination of how these trade-offs are influenced by the aforementioned variables. We demonstrate that a model's size is a critical determinant of these trade-offs, as larger models exhibit greater gains on certain tasks while suffering losses on others. Furthermore, we find that the domain of a task significantly impacts the trade-off landscape, with domain-specific tasks yielding superior improvements compared to domain-agnostic tasks. Finally, we observe that while higher-quality data enhances the magnitude of performance gains, it does not alter the fundamental nature of the trade-offs. These insights offer valuable guidance for practitioners seeking to optimize language model performance.

This study examines how legitimate peripheral participation (LPP) influences the learning objectives of novices within informal online communities. Utilizing a qualitative approach, we analyzed data from a Reddit-based community of young, aspiring writers. Our findings indicate that LPP serves as a vital mechanism for the pursuit of these learning goals. Specifically, we identified three primary modes of engagement—dialogue, observation, and co-optation—each contributing to the acquisition of distinct knowledge types. Furthermore, we discovered that the most active participants were those who most effectively leveraged LPP to meet their specific educational aims.

This study introduces a local density approximation tailored for the transcorrelated (TC) method, a many-body technique that has demonstrated superior accuracy over the random phase approximation (RPA) in modeling metallic systems. By employing a Gaussian process regression algorithm, we interpolate the TC kernel across various density parameters, enabling the calculation of TC energies for arbitrary electron densities. Our findings indicate that this new TC kernel yields results comparable to the RPA kernel, with deviations remaining within approximately 10%.

This study examines a perturbation scheme designed to address the challenges of location uncertainty in the context of the incompressible Euler equations. By employing a smoothing kernel, the proposed method ensures the preservation of specific quantities throughout the evolution, thereby guaranteeing a unique solution. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the scheme maintains the continuity equation and conservality of the inviscid kinetic energy. Additionally, we derive an estimate for the error in the solution, which is contingent upon the $L^1$ norm of the uncertainty distribution.

This paper introduces a new algorithm, SafeAPT, designed to adapt robotic policies from simulation to the real world while ensuring safety. SafePT operates by integrating a model predictive controller (MPC) with a robust reward function that penalizes unsafe actions. This mechanism allows SafePT to safely explore environments and identify policy failures, which are then used to refine the simulation-to-real model and improve the adaptation process. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of experiments involving a two-armed robotic manipulation task.

This study introduces a nonparametric test for regression functions that avoids the need for structural assumptions, such as linearity or monotonicity. The approach relies on a U-statistic derived from a kernel-based distance metric between the estimated regression function and the true, unknown function. The test's validity is established through a central limit theorem for U-statistics under the null hypothesis, while power is demonstrated via a concentration inequality for the estimated regression function under the alternative. The methodology is further illustrated through a case study analyzing the relationship between the number of employees and annual sales revenue in the retail sector.

This study investigates the efficacy of multilingual versus monolingual models for analyzing social media content. We evaluate these models across various tasks, including hate speech detection, multilingual NLP benchmarks, and multilingual word embeddings. Our findings indicate that multilingual models perform comparably to their monolingual counterparts, with performance gaps remaining minimal.

Functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) is a non-invasive imaging technique that captures brain activity by monitoring hemodynamic changes. While fMRI has been extensively utilized for diagnosing and monitoring various brain disorders, its application in machine learning is constrained by the high dimensionality of the data. This study introduces a novel deep learning framework designed to classify brain conditions using fMRI data. The proposed architecture employs a two-stage process: first, a 3D convolutional neural network extracts features from the input data, and second, a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network classifies these features. This hybrid CNN-LSTM model was evaluated on a dataset comprising 1,000 fMRI scans from 250 subjects across three categories: healthy controls, Alzheimer's disease, and mild cognitive impairment. The results demonstrate that the CNN-LSTM approach outperforms existing methods, achieving an accuracy of 90.5%.

This paper investigates the stability of linear systems under dissipative feedbacks, a framework prevalent in control theory. We introduce a novel methodology for convergence rate analysis that relies on the energy dissipation of the closed-loop system. Specifically, we derive the optimal convergence rate by maximizing a certain parameter subject to the closed-loop dissipation inequality, employing a semidefinite programming approach to solve this problem. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this calculated convergence rate is achievable.

This study introduces a boundary treatment approach for high-order numerical schemes that integrates the characteristics of high-order accuracy with the robustness of low-order methods. By employing a low-order numerical flux at boundaries, the proposed technique ensures stability and convergence for high-order interior schemes, while maintaining high-order accuracy in interior regions away from the boundary. The method's effectiveness is demonstrated through applications to both linear and nonlinear advection equations, as well as the Euler equations.

Valuation algebra serves as a powerful framework for representing and computing with uncertain knowledge, particularly when uncertainty cannot be precisely quantified. This paper extends that framework to credal sets—the collections of probability distributions that define our primary focus. We establish the fundamental operations for valuing credal sets, including combination, marginalization, and minimization. Furthermore, we demonstrate that these operations can be computed in linear time relative to the network's size. Finally, we provide a comprehensive analysis of the associated computational complexity.

We introduce a distance-based recommendation model that incorporates the Wasserstein distance to enhance performance. This approach is particularly effective for recommender systems where the Wasserstein metric is readily available. Furthermore, we provide a theoretical analysis of the proposed model's generalization error, establishing an upper bound that is tight up to logarithmic factors.

Non-Markovian dynamics are a key feature of open quantum systems, and the quantification of this property has been extensively studied. This paper introduces a non-Markovian channel characterized by quasi-entangling (quasi-ENM) operations, which differs from the standard GHZ-based entanglement (GAD) channel. While the GAD channel exhibits non-Markovian behavior regardless of the system's initial state, the quasi-ENM GAD channel only demonstrates such properties when the initial state is not GHZ. This distinction reveals a new type of non-Markovian behavior that does not rely solely on GHZ states. Furthermore, we examine the relationship between non-Markovianity and the preservation of quantum correlations within the quasi-ENM GAD channel. Our findings indicate that non-Markovianity can effectively protect quantum correlations in this context, offering a viable strategy for maintaining entanglement.

This paper introduces Contrastive Representation Augmentation with Random Augmentation and Label noise (CCRAL), a new technique designed to enhance model generalization on unseen testing data. CCRAL operates by generating pseudo-labels for augmented samples and subsequently applying contrastive learning to align representations of identical samples while separating those of different samples. The method's simplicity and effectiveness are demonstrated through its application to the CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 datasets, where it achieves significant performance gains. Furthermore, CCRAL is shown to be highly effective in mitigating the effects of label noise, a common issue in real-world data.

Creating semantic maps is crucial for enabling robots to perform tasks autonomously, yet the process is labor-intensive and prone to errors. To address this, we introduce a new framework for automatically assigning semantic labels to 2D maps. Our approach utilizes a hybrid strategy that combines a pre-trained, large-scale knowledge base with a small, domain-specific knowledge source. This paper introduces Rikudo, a newly developed puzzle variant, and establishes a polynomial-time algorithm for solving instances where all even numbers are placed correctly. The analysis demonstrates that the puzzle is solvable in polynomial time specifically when odd numbers are positioned within the first six columns.

This paper introduces a novel algorithm for solving the optimal transport problem, a cornerstone of machine learning. Our approach leverages the Sinkhorn's algorithm, a method known for its efficiency in addressing large-scale linear programming tasks. We demonstrate that this technique can be reformulated as a discrete gradient descent step applied to a convex objective function, a structure that facilitates the development of accelerated variants. Furthermore, we establish theoretical guarantees regarding the algorithm's convergence rate. Empirical results indicate that these proposed methods outperform existing state-of-the-art approaches.

The quasar, located at a redshift of $z=0.894$, is lensed by a radio galaxy at $z=0.604$. This study addresses a Cauchy problem associated with a $q$-fractional differential equation, where the $q$-derivative is defined by the parameter $q \in (0,1)$. The $q$-fractional derivative is constructed using the standard fractional derivative and the $q$-derivative. By employing the difference method, the authors demonstrate that the Cauchy problem admits a unique solution. Furthermore, an algorithm for approximating this solution is introduced, and numerical experiments are conducted to validate the findings.

This study investigates the phonon Hall effect (PHE) in dielectric materials, focusing on the impact of magnetic fields on phonon Hall conductivity (PHC). We demonstrate that a magnetic field can induce a non-zero PHC in systems with C2v symmetry, a phenomenon arising from the interplay between phonon group velocity and the magnetic field. Furthermore, we analyze the impact of anisotropic phonon scattering on the magnitude of PHC. Our findings indicate that anisotropic scattering can enhance the PHC by several orders of magnitude, offering a viable method for boosting PHE efficiency.

Wide-field imaging systems are increasingly utilized in astronomy, yet they face challenges with acquisition times and data processing. We introduce a novel "nod and shuffle" approach designed to enhance both the speed of data collection and the efficiency of processing. This technique involves moving the detector in a specific pattern to capture multiple images of the same field region, thereby enabling the reconstruction of a single, high-resolution, wide-field image. We demonstrate that this method significantly boosts acquisition speeds by a factor of 10 to 100, depending on the specific configuration. Furthermore, we show that the processing phase can be streamlined by a factor of 10 through the application of a fast Fourier transform.

This work introduces matrix analogues of the Baumgartner-Daners and Daners inequalities. We establish their validity within the context of bounded linear operators acting on Hilbert spaces and subsequently examine the conditions under which equality holds.

This study examines the behavior of the averaged null energy condition (ANEC) within the context of spheriously symmetric black hole formation and evaporation. Our findings indicate that while the ANEC is violated during the collapse phase, it remains satisfied throughout the subsequent evaporation process.

In a four-dimensional Conformal Field Theory (CFT) featuring an irrelevant operator with integer conformal dimension $\Delta$, the trace anomaly acquires an extra term proportional to $\left(\partial^2\phi\right)^2$. This contribution necessitates a redefinition of the $a$- and $c$-central charges, which now depend on $\Delta$. We demonstrate that these updated central charges adhere to the $a-c\gtrless0$ inequality and the $c$-theorem. Furthermore, the $c$-theorem's proof is extended to this framework by adapting the standard argument of Osborn and McFadden, which originally relied on the energy-momentum tensor's positivity.

This study introduces a maturity model for analyzing Industrial Control Systems (ICS) testbeds, designed to evaluate their capabilities and guide the development of a tailored assessment methodology. The research details the model's structure, including its hierarchical maturity levels and associated key performance indicators (KPIs). Additionally, the paper outlines a specific framework for developing the measurement framework and defining the relevant metrics. To validate the model's practicality, it is applied to assess an existing ICS testbed, demonstrating its utility. The study concludes by identifying critical areas for future investigation.

Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) has garnered significant attention in recent years, particularly for its potential to solve intricate challenges in robotics and autonomous driving. However, existing MARL methods often struggle with scalability and generalization. This paper introduces a novel MARL framework leveraging greedy-based value representation (GVR) to enhance performance. GVR utilizes a greedy algorithm to derive a compact value representation of the state, which is then integrated into the Q-network to boost learning efficiency. Furthermore, we employ a dynamic action space reduction strategy that narrows the action space based on the GVR, thereby accelerating convergence. Experimental results on the StarCraft II benchmark demonstrate that our approach surpasses current state-of-the-art methods.

Although numerous studies have identified gender stereotypes in language, few have established standardized metrics for quantifying them. This paper introduces StereoSet, a novel dataset designed to measure stereotypical biases across four distinct domains: gender, race, age, profession, and personal traits. To ensure robustness, we developed a set of 100 word pairs from each domain, creating 200 unique sentence structures. These sentences are evaluated using a pre-trained BERT model to determine the likelihood of a specific word appearing in a particular context. By comparing the probability scores for each word within its paired alternatives, we generate a quantitative measure of stereotype strength. We conducted extensive experiments on existing pre-trained models, revealing that while these models excel at grammatical correctness, they often fail to capture the nuanced semantic associations between words. To address this, we propose a new architecture trained specifically on our StereoSet data, demonstrating that our approach significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art methods in mitigating word-level gender biases.

This paper introduces a Contextual Multi-Armed Bandit (CMAB) framework designed to learn tilt update policies for optimizing network traffic. The proposed approach integrates the contextual CMAB framework with the gradient method to achieve rapid convergence. Theoretically, we demonstrate that the proposed algorithm converges to the optimal tilt update policy. Furthermore, simulations on a real-world network environment confirm the effectiveness of this approach.

This analysis determines the CKM angle $\gamma$ by examining the decays $B^+ \to D K^+$ and $B^+ \to \bar{D} K^+$. The $B^+ \to D K^+$ decays are reconstructed using $K_S^0 \pi^+ \pi^-$, $K^+ K^-$, and $K^+ K^- \pi^+$ final states of the $D$ meson. The $B^+ \to \bar{D} K^+$ decays are identified through $K_S^0 \pi^+ \pi^-$, $K^+ K^- \pi^+$, and $K_S^0 K^- \pi^+$ final states of the $\bar{D}$ meson. The study utilizes a data sample of 38 fb$^{-1}$ collected by the LHCb experiment at center-of-mass energies of 7 and 8 TeV. The measured value for $\gamma$ is $69.4^{+4.0}_{-3.6}$ degrees at 95.5% confidence, with an uncertainty of $4.0_{-3.6}^{+4.0}$ degrees. Additionally, the CP-violation phase difference for $B^+ \to \bar{D} K^+$ decays is found to be $0.3 \pm 1.

This work extends the classical concept of $k$-convexity to complex settings, thereby characterizing convex bodies through their projections and sections. We demonstrate that complex symmetry functions as a fundamental component in this characterization. Furthermore, we establish that these complex convex bodies possess non-degenerate Hessian operators, which enables us to define a broad category of functions as complex convex bodies.

The rise of data markets has introduced a new paradigm for personal data transactions, one that relies on the assumption that individuals act as rational agents capable of consistently maximizing their utility. This paper investigates whether such markets can truly thrive by examining personal data transactions through the lens of behavioral economics. We conducted a qualitative study involving 20 interviews with participants who had engaged in various personal data transactions. Our analysis reveals that the current market model fails to account for the complexities of human decision-making, as layperson behaviors often defy existing economic frameworks. Consequently, we propose a new framework grounded in behavioral economics that better explains these observed behaviors. Finally, we discuss the critical implications of these findings for the design of future data markets.

This study introduces a deep learning approach for detecting the optimal timing offset in Frequency-Offseted Nyquist signaling (FTN). By leveraging deep neural networks, the proposed method significantly lowers detection complexity and mitigates the impact of channel noise. We evaluate the system's performance using Root Raised Cosine (RRC) signaling with a rolloff factor of 0.8. The results demonstrate that the network achieves high accuracy in identifying timing offsets, even under severe channel conditions.

This work examines effect algebras equipped with both an order and a topology, analyzing their interplay. We demonstrate that for any complete atomic distributive lattice, the Frink ideal topology and the order topology of the corresponding effect distributive lattice coincide if and only if the lattice is effect. Additionally, we provide an example of a finite non-distributive effect algebra that possesses precisely one open set: the entire algebra itself.

This study introduces SaliencyMix, a novel data augmentation technique designed to enhance object detection model performance. The method operates by merging two images based on their saliency maps, which are generated using a pre-trained network. The resulting images are subsequently employed to train a detection model. The proposed approach is straightforward to implement and computationally efficient, as it relies on the saliency maps of just one image. Theoretical analysis confirms that SaliencyMix achieves generalization by expanding the training dataset's diversity. Empirical results demonstrate that the method improves the accuracy of both two-stage and one-stage detectors. The associated code can be accessed at https://github.com/zhengyuan0214/SaliencyMix.

In 1988, Vershik and Kerov fully enumerated the indecomposable positive traces on infinite Iwahiri–Hecke algebras, categorized by their rank. This research extends that classification specifically to the case of odd rank within the context of affine type $A$.

This study investigates the alignment parameter, a metric designed to detect large-scale anisotropies in the intrinsic shapes of galaxies. We introduce a novel estimator for this parameter that leverages the cross-correlation between the alignment-sensitive cosmic shear three-point function and the galaxy bispectrum. By employing a pseudo-Cl formalism, we demonstrate that this approach is capable of isolating the alignment signal from intrinsic shape correlations. Furthermore, we evaluate the sensitivity of our proposed estimator to various systematic effects, including intrinsic alignments, photometric redshift errors, and shear calibration inaccuracies. Our findings indicate that, under ideal observational conditions, this new estimator can achieve a 10% precision on the alignment parameter within a decade of cosmic time.

Soft-deformable particle systems, such as elastomers and biological tissues, exhibit complex behaviors under cyclic loading, including hysteresis and plastic deformation. This study investigates how internal microstructural organization influences the macroscopic stress-strain response of these materials. Utilizing a numerical framework based on a coarse-grained model of a network of interacting dumbbells, we simulate a material with a microstructure that evolves during cyclic deformation. Our findings reveal that these systems display a memory effect characterized by a delayed response to strain reversal, a phenomenon that intensifies with higher applied strain. We attribute this to the formation of a persistent, anisotropic microstructure that remains imprinted in the system even after load removal. Furthermore, we demonstrate that these memory effects can be harnessed to create tunable, non-reciprocal mechanical systems, such as a frictionless, non-retractable "stick-slip" slider.

We present a computational investigation into the thermodynamic stability of phase transitions in gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) utilizing a machine learning (ML) potential trained on density functional theory (DFT) data. Our findings indicate that, contrary to predictions based on classical potentials, the AuNPs remain thermodynamically stable in the face-centered cubic (fcc) phase even at the smallest scales examined. Furthermore, the study reveals that the melting point of these nanoparticles is not a monotonic function of size; instead, it exhibits a non-monotonic trend, rising to a peak at approximately 1.5 nm. This behavior is attributed to the coexistence of the face-centered cubic (fcc) and hexagonal close-packed (hcp) phases at this critical size.

This paper examines the impact of relaxing standard differentiability requirements on the analysis of quasi-linear elliptic boundary value problems defined on manifolds. We demonstrate that our modified approach yields significant advantages, particularly regarding the identification of the precise minimal smoothness level required for boundary data to guarantee both existence and uniqueness of solutions. Furthermore, we illustrate that this framework is broadly applicable to various geometric contexts, encompassing both Riemannian and contact manifolds.

This study examines a minimal $U(1)_X$ gauge extension of the Standard Model that resolves anomalies through the minimal number of additional fields: three heavy right-handed neutrinos. The $U(1)_X$ charge assignments are designed to ensure the model remains anomaly-free while permitting the Standard Model's charged fermions to acquire masses via a singlet Higgs mechanism. The model is characterized by a distinctive flavor structure, where the horizontal gauge symmetry induces a non-trivial mixing matrix between quarks and anti-leptons, thereby generating significant flavor-violating effects. The analysis investigates the phenomenology of this framework, focusing on flavor-changing neutral current (FCNC) processes, the generation of neutrino masses, and the potential for a singlet Higgs boson discovery at future colliders.

This study establishes several identities related to $(h; q)$-Genocchi polynomials and numbers by utilizing the $(h; q)$-Genocchi generating function. Furthermore, we demonstrate that these results validate the previously conjectured values for $G_q(-n; -1)$, thereby providing a proof for $-n$ values with $n \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{0\}$.

This study introduces a novel reinforcement learning framework for addressing nonstationary problems characterized by evolving average rewards. By leveraging a novel regret metric that accounts for the cumulative variation in these average rewards, the proposed approach offers a versatile and adaptable solution. This methodology is applicable across various scenarios, including environments with shifting state and action rewards, rewards that fluctuate based on the current state-action pair, and situations involving delayed rewards. The theoretical analysis demonstrates that the proposed algorithm achieves the optimal regret bound for general nonstationary Markov decision processes. Furthermore, the study provides a practical regret upper bound tailored for linear MDPs, which is shown to be nearly optimal.

Causal inference has become a central focus in research across numerous disciplines. While randomized controlled trials (RCTs) are the gold standard for establishing causality, observational studies remain prevalent. A critical challenge in both settings is determining whether an outcome is caused by the treatment, which is typically quantified using causal odds ratios (CORs). This paper introduces a method to estimate the COR for binary treatment and binary outcomes, even when unmeasured confounding exists. The approach relies on a unmeasured confounding model that assumes a specific parametric form for the unmeasured confounding odds ratio, allowing for the derivation of a closed-form estimator. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that the method is unbiased and consistent under correct model specification. Furthermore, simulation studies confirm the method's validity and illustrate its application using data from a study on the association between statin use and the risk of developing diabetes.

Autoencoders are widely employed in machine learning for tasks including dimensionality reduction, generative modeling, and representation learning. This study introduces a novel autoencoder architecture grounded in invertible layers, designed to enhance performance in both generative modeling and dimensionality reduction. Our approach involves substituting the standard bottleneck layer with a set of invertible layers, thereby creating a bijective mapping between the latent space and the input space. This design ensures that the latent representation is uniquely recoverable from the input. Our findings indicate that autoencoders built with this method achieve superior log-likelihood scores and produce higher-quality samples compared to those utilizing bottleneck layers. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this architecture supports effective dimensionality reduction.

Smart cities are increasingly generating vast amounts of data, necessitating visualization tools that enable the creation of interactive, dynamic, and personalized analytical visual representations. This paper introduces a new visual system designed to support the interactive exploration of urban data. The system's core capabilities include the ability to define specific user personas and a comprehensive set of visual representations that facilitate the discovery of data insights.

This study introduces optimal geometric multigrid preconditioners for linear systems arising from hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HdG) discretizations of elliptic partial differential equations (PDEs). By employing a hierarchical mesh reduction strategy, we develop two distinct multigrid approaches: one rooted in the Ritz projection and another utilizing a hierarchical high-order reconstruction technique. We demonstrate that both preconditioners achieve optimal convergence rates in the H-norm of the discrete space, provided the mesh size is sufficiently fine. Furthermore, we analyze the impact of varying polynomial degrees on grid convergence and validate our findings with numerical experiments.

The E-value serves as a unifying framework for quantifying unmeasured confounding in causal inference. This paper extends the concept to scenarios involving data with missing values, enabling the measurement of confounding robustness for causal findings across both missing-at-random (MAR) and monotone missingness contexts. Specifically, we derive a formula for the E-value that accounts for confounding robustness under MAR assumptions, as well as under constraints on the proportion of completely missing observations. We demonstrate that our proposed approach yields tighter E-values compared to existing methods. Furthermore, we illustrate how these extended E-values can inform sensitivity analyses for missing data.

In crossover trials with few participants, missing data poses a significant challenge, as the resulting uncertainty can substantially compromise the reliability of treatment effect estimates. This study introduces a Bayesian approach to address this issue, utilizing informative priors to leverage data from fully observed periods to inform imputations of missing outcomes. By applying this method to a small-scale asthma crossover trial, we demonstrate that it yields more precise estimates of treatment effects compared to standard analysis techniques.

We demonstrate that the $A_n$-structure on the geometric realization of a category's nerve is determined by its simplicial composition of simplices. Specifically, we provide an explicit description of the resulting simplices based on the structure of the category. This result extends a theorem by Fresse, which characterizes the $A_\infty$-structure on the nerve of an $A_\infty$-category.

This paper introduces a novel physical unclonable function (PUF) based on DRAM. The system's core relies on a 256-bit challenge-response key, which is processed through a 256-bit secret key to generate a 256-bit response. The proposed DRAM PUF demonstrates superior robustness and throughput compared to current state-of-the-art DRAM PUFs. The study also examines the impact of various parameters on the PUF's reliability and security. The authors further analyze the PUF's resistance to side-channel attacks, including differential power analysis (DPA) and differential electromagnetic analysis (DEMA). The findings indicate that the proposed DRAM PUF offers enhanced resistance to these attacks compared to existing methods.

This paper presents Virtualized Network Function Orchestration (VNF-O) in Haskell, a functional programming language. Haskell's features, particularly its immutability, align well with the dynamic nature of cloud computing, making it well-suited for VNF-O. The paper details a Haskell-based model for VNF-O, focusing on the abstract resource model and the abstract service model. Additionally, it explores the Haskell-specific extensions required to adapt the 3GPP ETSI standards for implementation.

The rise of topological quantum computing has spurred the development of increasingly complex topological quantum gates. This study proposes a scalable benchmarking framework for these gates, utilizing the toric code to gauge the performance of individual gates and the surface code to assess the entire system. We introduce a method to calculate benchmarking success probabilities for both small and large logical qubit configurations, alongside a simplified analytical approach for estimating success probabilities of gate sequences. Furthermore, we explore the implications of these techniques for topological quantum computation.

The Universal Worker System (UWS) is a distributed framework designed to facilitate job execution within large-scale computing clusters. It enables the delegation of tasks to remote workers, who then return results to the master node. This paper introduces a novel approach for selecting workers based on their historical performance metrics, specifically targeting the minimization of total job completion time. We demonstrate that this worker selection problem can be modeled as a variant of the Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP). Furthermore, we introduce an efficient algorithm for solving this TSP variant and evaluate its performance against a baseline strategy that assigns jobs to the fastest available worker.

This study introduces a new framework for applying blockchain-enabled machine learning (BM) to wireless communications and networking systems. We examine how blockchain technology can enhance learning capabilities within these domains and outline the specific challenges involved. Furthermore, we present a comprehensive survey of recent advancements in the integration of machine learning with blockchain for such systems. The paper concludes by highlighting future research directions and potential applications.

The detection of oxygen (O2) and ozone (O3) in terrestrial exoplanet atmospheres is often considered a potential biosignature, yet their presence alone does not definitively indicate life. This study investigates how host star temperature influences the relationship between O2 and O3, specifically examining the impact of stellar UV flux on O3 generation. We employed a 1D radiative-convective model to simulate atmospheres of Earth-analog planets under varying stellar conditions, including G-type (Sun-like), K-type, and M-type stars. Our results indicate that for planets orbiting cooler stars, the traditional link between O2 and O3 is disrupted due to elevated UV flux, which drives O3 production through non-biological mechanisms. Consequently, O3 levels can reach significant concentrations even in the absence of life. This finding suggests that O2-O3 correlations should not be relied upon as biosignatures for terrestrial exoplanets orbiting stars cooler than the Sun.

Surface currents are widely recognized for their robustness in the presence of disorder, a trait that extends to both bosonic and fermionic systems. This study demonstrates that such currents can also be realized in the absence of disorder within non-Hermitian systems. Specifically, we examine a two-dimensional lattice featuring a non-Hermitian skin effect, where the emergence of surface currents is driven by the topological properties of the bulk. We show that these currents are characterized by a non-trivial bulk invariant, specifically the bulk non-Hermitian winding number. Furthermore, we analyze the stability of these currents against disorder and non-reciprocity, confirming that they remain robust against both. Finally, we explore the potential for utilizing these currents in the context of non-Hermitian topological quantum computing.

This study introduces a multilingual neural machine translation (mNMT) model designed for the medical domain, which incorporates domain adaptation. The proposed approach utilizes a domain-adapted pre-trained model and integrates a domain-adapted self-attention mechanism. Experimental results indicate that this domain-adapted mNMT significantly outperforms an out-of-domain model in the medical domain, achieving BLEU score gains of 1.0 and 1.3 for English-to-German and English-to-French translation tasks, respectively.

This study examines the generation of both solitary and shock waves within a magnetized, electron-positron-ion plasma containing negative dust grains. Utilizing the reductive perturbation technique, we derived the non-linear ion-acoustic dust ion acoustic (LIA) equation to analyze these phenomena. The analysis reveals that dust acoustic solitary waves (DSWs) and dust acoustic shock waves (DASWs) can coexist, with the ion fluid temperature and the degree of electron non-thermalization serving as critical factors in their formation. Additionally, we numerically investigated the impact of dust grain inertia and the non-linear parameter on the DSWs and DASWs characteristics. Our findings indicate that increased dust grain inertia and the non-linear parameter lead to heightened values for the DSWs and DASWs amplitudes.

We introduce a novel contrastive sentence representation learning approach grounded in the contrastive context prediction (CCP) task. Unlike previous methods that rely on sentence prediction, our approach leverages the contextual information between words to achieve a more fine-grained understanding of sentence semantics. To facilitate this, we develop a new architecture that integrates a masked language model with a transformer encoder specifically to reconstruct the contrasted sentence context. We further demonstrate that our method, which is language-agnostic, effectively supports multilingual sentence representation learning by training jointly across multiple languages. Experimental results indicate that our approach outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques in multilingual settings, particularly in scenarios with limited data.

This paper introduces a novel multimodal learning framework designed to optimize the performance of slower modalities. We achieve this by leveraging the prototypical learning paradigm to derive class-specific representations from each modality, thereby guiding the learning process. Specifically, we propose a method termed "Prototypical Modality Rebalance" (PMR), which recalibrates the contribution of each modality during training. PMR dynamically adjusts the learning pace to ensure faster and slower modalities are trained at comparable rates. Experimental results across various benchmarks demonstrate that our approach consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods.

This study introduces a novel command recognition framework that integrates a small Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with a Transformer-based DNN (TT-DNN). The proposed architecture leverages the CNN to extract features from the input, which are subsequently processed by the TT-DNN to generate final predictions. Experimental results indicate that the CNN+(TT-DNN) model achieves superior parameter efficiency compared to a traditional, standalone CNN model while maintaining equivalent recognition accuracy.

This study investigates the control of deterministic evolution in a three-level quantum system driven by a specific non-Hermitian Hamiltonian. We demonstrate that by adjusting the parameters of the surrounding driving field, the system's evolution can be precisely regulated to achieve a desired outcome. Furthermore, we propose a method to manipulate the non-triviality of the Hamiltonian's spectrum through the excitation of an intermediate auxiliary level.

We introduce a novel plasmonic solar cell design that utilizes a single nanoparticle to convert incident light into electrical current. This device employs a single aluminum nanoparticle positioned on a dielectric layer above a gold back reflector, with a thin indium tin oxide (ITO) film acting as the electrode. The photocurrent is generated through the photoelectric effect, where electrons are emitted from the heated particle by absorbed photons and collected by the ITO layer. Our analysis demonstrates that aluminum nanoparticles achieve superior efficiency compared to gold or silver counterparts, reaching a peak of 14.4% conversion efficiency at a 550 nm wavelength. Additionally, we examine the impact of particle size, incident angle, and polarization on efficiency, revealing that vertically oriented polarization yields higher performance.

This paper introduces a new algebra of binary relations that integrates linear-time modal dynamic logic, specifically designed to model the sequential application of relations. By combining this algebra with a theory of computation, we establish a framework for analyzing computational processes as sequences of binary relations. These relational operations correspond to the fundamental mechanisms of computation: state transitions, branching choices, and deterministic evolution. The work demonstrates that this algebraic system is complete and sound relative to the linear-time modal logic of computation, thereby establishing its capacity to serve as a robust logical framework for reasoning about computational processes.
